Prime & Composite Numbers.q: What is the smallest prime number?
Prime & Composite Numbers.explain: 2 is the smallest prime number — and the only even prime.

Prime & Composite Numbers.q: Is 1 a prime number?
Prime & Composite Numbers.explain: 1 has only one factor (itself), so it is neither prime nor composite.

Prime & Composite Numbers.q: Is 2 an odd or even prime number?
Prime & Composite Numbers.explain: 2 is the only even number that is prime — all other primes are odd.

Prime & Composite Numbers.q: Which of these is a composite number?
Prime & Composite Numbers.explain: 21 = 3×7, so it has more than two factors (1, 3, 7, 21), making it composite.

Prime & Composite Numbers.q: How many factors does a composite number have? (type "more than 2" or a similar phrase)
Prime & Composite Numbers.explain: Composite numbers always have more than two factors.

Prime & Composite Numbers.q: Which of these numbers is NEITHER prime nor composite?
Prime & Composite Numbers.explain: 1 has only one factor, so it doesn’t fit either category.

Prime & Composite Numbers.q: Arrange these numbers, listing the PRIME ones first, then composite ones:
Prime & Composite Numbers.explain: Primes first (5, 3), then composites (9, 8).

Prime & Composite Numbers.q: List the factors of 13.
Prime & Composite Numbers.explain: 13 is prime, so its only factors are 1 and 13.

Prime & Composite Numbers.q: What method helps find all primes up to a given number by crossing out multiples?
Prime & Composite Numbers.explain: The Sieve of Eratosthenes crosses out multiples of each prime to reveal the primes that remain.

Prime & Composite Numbers.q: Is 17 prime or composite? (type prime or composite)
Prime & Composite Numbers.explain: 17 has only two factors: 1 and 17.

Prime & Composite Numbers.q: Which of these is a pair of TWIN primes (primes differing by 2)?
Prime & Composite Numbers.explain: 5 and 7 are both prime and differ by exactly 2, making them twin primes.

Prime & Composite Numbers.q: Is 91 prime or composite? (Hint: 91 = 7×13) (type prime or composite)
Prime & Composite Numbers.explain: 91 = 7×13, so it has factors besides 1 and itself, making it composite.

Prime & Composite Numbers.q: How many prime numbers are there between 1 and 10?
Prime & Composite Numbers.explain: The primes between 1 and 10 are 2, 3, 5, 7 — that is 4 primes.

Prime & Composite Numbers.q: A teacher gives out 23 candies and wants to split them into equal groups (more than 1 group, fewer than 23 candies each) with none left over. Is this possible?
Prime & Composite Numbers.explain: 23 is a prime number, so its only factors are 1 and 23 — it cannot be split into smaller equal groups.

Prime & Composite Numbers.q: A gardener has 36 flower pots and wants to arrange them into equal rows of more than 1 pot per row. Is this possible, given 36 is composite?
opts: Yes, in several different row sizes
Only if there are exactly 2 rows
Prime & Composite Numbers.explain: Since 36 is composite, it has many factors (1,2,3,4,6,9,12,18,36), allowing several valid equal-row arrangements.

Prime & Composite Numbers.q: A security code uses a 2-digit prime number for a locker. Name one possible prime number between 10 and 20 that could be used.
Prime & Composite Numbers.explain: Primes between 10 and 20 include 11, 13, 17, 19 — 11 is one valid answer.

Prime & Composite Numbers.q: A number puzzle says "I am a 2-digit number, I am prime, and the sum of my digits is 8." Which number fits?
Prime & Composite Numbers.explain: 17 is prime, and 1+7=8, matching both clues.

Prime & Composite Numbers.q: A class is sorting number cards into a prime pile and a composite pile. Arrange these cards in the order: prime, prime, composite, composite.
Prime & Composite Numbers.explain: 2 and 3 are prime; 9 and 10 are composite — order: 2, 3, 9, 10.

Prime Factorization.q: What is prime factorization?
opts: Writing a number as a sum of primes
Writing a number as a product of only prime numbers
Listing all factors of a number
Prime Factorization.explain: Prime factorization means expressing a number as a product made entirely of prime numbers.

Prime Factorization.q: What is the prime factorization of 12? (use × between numbers)
What is the prime factorization of 20?
Which method uses branches that split a number until only primes remain?
Prime Factorization.explain: The factor tree method splits a number into smaller factors repeatedly until every branch ends in a prime.

Prime Factorization.q: In the repeated division method, which prime number should you try first?
Prime Factorization.explain: Always start with the smallest prime, 2, and only move to the next prime when 2 no longer divides exactly.

Prime Factorization.q: What is the prime factorization of 30?
Is the prime factorization of a number always unique?
opts: Yes, every number has exactly one set of prime factors
No, it changes depending on the method used
Prime Factorization.explain: No matter which method you use, every number breaks down into the same unique combination of primes.

Prime Factorization.q: What is the prime factorization of 50?
What is the prime factorization of 100?
Arrange the steps of the factor tree method for the number 28:
Prime Factorization.explain: Split 28 into 4×7, then split 4 further into 2×2, leaving all branches as primes: 2,2,7.

Prime Factorization.q: What is the prime factorization of 16?
Why can a prime number itself not be broken down further in a factor tree?
opts: It has no factors at all
Its only factors are 1 and itself, so it is already prime
It is always an odd number
Prime Factorization.explain: A prime number has exactly two factors (1 and itself), so it cannot be split into smaller factors besides 1.

Prime Factorization.q: What is the prime factorization of 63?
A student breaks 84 into a factor tree and gets the final primes 2, 2, 3, 7. Is this correct?
opts: No, a number can only have 2 prime factors

Prime Factorization.q: A locker code is created by multiplying three prime numbers: 2, 3, and 11. What is the code?
A baker wants to break 90 cookies into equal trays where the tray size is a prime factor of 90. Name one possible tray size.
Prime Factorization.explain: 90=2×3×3×5, so valid prime-factor tray sizes are 2, 3, or 5.

Prime Factorization.q: A number is built using the primes 2 (twice) and 5 (once). What is the number?
A teacher demonstrates the repeated division method for 40. Arrange the divisions in the correct order:
Prime Factorization.explain: Keep dividing by 2 while possible (40→20→10→5), then divide by 5 to reach 1, collecting primes 2,2,2,5.

Prime Factorization.q: A number’s prime factorization is given as 2×2×3×3×3. What is the number?
Which of these is the correct prime factorization of 75?

HCF and LCM.q: What does HCF stand for?
HCF and LCM.explain: HCF = Highest Common Factor, the largest number dividing two or more numbers exactly.

HCF and LCM.q: What does LCM stand for?
HCF and LCM.explain: LCM = Lowest Common Multiple, the smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers.

HCF and LCM.q: What is the HCF of 6 and 9?
HCF and LCM.explain: Factors of 6: 1,2,3,6. Factors of 9: 1,3,9. Common factors: 1,3 — highest is 3.

HCF and LCM.q: What is the LCM of 2 and 3?
HCF and LCM.explain: Multiples of 2: 2,4,6... Multiples of 3: 3,6,9... Lowest common multiple is 6.

HCF and LCM.q: The HCF of two numbers is always:
opts: Smaller than or equal to both numbers
HCF and LCM.explain: HCF can never be bigger than the smaller of the two numbers — it is always smaller than or equal to both.

HCF and LCM.q: The LCM of two numbers is always:
opts: Greater than or equal to both numbers
HCF and LCM.explain: LCM is always greater than or equal to the larger of the two numbers.

HCF and LCM.q: What is the HCF of two numbers that have no common factor other than 1, like 8 and 9?
HCF and LCM.explain: When numbers share no factor besides 1, their HCF is 1 — they are called co-prime.

HCF and LCM.q: What is the LCM of 5 and 10?
HCF and LCM.explain: 10 is already a multiple of 5, so the lowest common multiple of 5 and 10 is 10 itself.

HCF and LCM.q: What is the HCF of 12 and 18?
HCF and LCM.explain: Factors of 12: 1,2,3,4,6,12. Factors of 18: 1,2,3,6,9,18. Common factors: 1,2,3,6 — highest is 6.

HCF and LCM.q: What is the LCM of 4 and 6?
HCF and LCM.explain: Multiples of 4: 4,8,12... Multiples of 6: 6,12,18... Lowest common multiple is 12.

HCF and LCM.q: When two numbers have an HCF of 1, what are they called?
HCF and LCM.explain: Numbers with HCF=1 (no common factor besides 1) are called co-prime numbers.

HCF and LCM.q: Arrange the steps to find the HCF of 16 and 24 using common factors:
HCF and LCM.explain: List both factor sets, then pick the highest common one: HCF(16,24)=8.

HCF and LCM.q: What is the HCF of 15 and 25?
HCF and LCM.explain: Factors of 15: 1,3,5,15. Factors of 25: 1,5,25. Common factors: 1,5 — highest is 5.

HCF and LCM.q: What is the LCM of 7 and 14?
HCF and LCM.explain: 14 is already a multiple of 7, so LCM(7,14)=14.

HCF and LCM.q: What is the LCM of 9 and 12?
HCF and LCM.explain: Multiples of 9: 9,18,27,36... Multiples of 12: 12,24,36... Lowest common multiple is 36.

HCF and LCM.q: Two ribbons of length 18cm and 24cm need to be cut into equal pieces with no leftover. What is the LONGEST possible piece length?
HCF and LCM.explain: The longest equal piece size is the HCF of 18 and 24, which is 6cm.

HCF and LCM.q: Two traffic lights blink every 10 seconds and every 15 seconds. After how many seconds will they blink together again?
HCF and LCM.explain: The lights blink together again after the LCM of 10 and 15, which is 30 seconds.

HCF and LCM.q: A teacher wants to split 20 boys and 30 girls into the largest possible equal-sized groups with no students left over. How many students should be in each group?
HCF and LCM.explain: The largest equal group size is the HCF of 20 and 30, which is 10.

HCF and LCM.q: Two friends visit the library every 6 days and every 8 days respectively. If they both visited today, after how many days will they both visit again on the same day?
HCF and LCM.explain: They will visit together again after the LCM of 6 and 8, which is 24 days.

HCF and LCM.q: A shop wants to pack 12 pencils and 18 erasers into identical kits using the largest possible number of kits with no items left over. Arrange the steps to solve this:
items: The HCF of 12 and 18 is 6, so 6 kits can be made
List factors of 12: 1,2,3,4,6,12 and factors of 18: 1,2,3,6,9,18
Find the highest common factor of 12 and 18
HCF and LCM.explain: List the factors, find the highest common one (6), which gives the maximum number of identical kits.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: To find HCF using prime factorization, you should multiply:
opts: Only the primes common to both, using the smaller power
Only the primes NOT common to both
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: HCF uses only the common primes, taking the smaller power if a prime repeats.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: To find LCM using prime factorization, you should multiply:
opts: All primes appearing in either number, using the highest power
Only primes from the smaller number
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: LCM uses every prime that appears in either number, taking the highest power it appears with.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: 12=2×2×3 and 18=2×3×3. What is the HCF using prime factorization?
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: Common primes: one 2 and one 3 (both numbers have at least these). HCF=2×3=6.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: 12=2×2×3 and 18=2×3×3. What is the LCM using prime factorization?
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: Highest powers: 2×2 (from 12) and 3×3 (from 18). LCM=2×2×3×3=36.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: 20=2×2×5 and 30=2×3×5. What is the HCF using prime factorization?
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: Common primes: one 2 and one 5. HCF=2×5=10.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: 20=2×2×5 and 30=2×3×5. What is the LCM using prime factorization?
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: Highest powers: 2×2 (from 20), one 3 (from 30), one 5. LCM=2×2×3×5=60.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: Why is prime factorization often faster for finding HCF/LCM of large numbers?
opts: It avoids listing every single factor
It only works for even numbers
It skips the need for multiplication
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: Breaking into primes is systematic and avoids the risk of missing a factor when listing all factors of a large number.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: 8=2×2×2 and 12=2×2×3. What is the HCF using prime factorization?
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: Common primes: 2×2 (both have at least two 2’s). HCF=2×2=4.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: 8=2×2×2 and 12=2×2×3. What is the LCM using prime factorization?
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: Highest powers: 2×2×2 (from 8) and one 3 (from 12). LCM=2×2×2×3=24.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: Arrange the steps to find HCF(45,60) using prime factorization:
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: Break both into primes, find the common ones (3 and 5), then multiply them: HCF=15.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: If two numbers are co-prime (share no common prime factors), what is their HCF using this method?
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: With no shared primes, there is nothing to multiply for HCF besides 1.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: If two numbers are co-prime, how do you find their LCM using prime factorization?
opts: Multiply all primes from both — which equals their product
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: Since there are no shared primes to avoid repeating, the LCM of co-prime numbers is simply their product.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: 14=2×7 and 21=3×7. What is the HCF using prime factorization?
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: The only common prime is 7. HCF=7.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: 14=2×7 and 21=3×7. What is the LCM using prime factorization?
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: All primes needed: 2, 3, 7 (no repeats needed since each appears once in either number). LCM=2×3×7=42.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: 16=2×2×2×2 and 24=2×2×2×3. What is the HCF using prime factorization?
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: Common primes: 2×2×2 (both have at least three 2’s). HCF=2×2×2=8.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: Two pieces of fabric measuring 28cm and 42cm (28=2×2×7, 42=2×3×7) need to be cut into equal pieces with no leftover, using the LONGEST possible piece. What is this length, using prime factorization?
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: Common primes: one 2 and one 7. HCF=2×7=14cm.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: Two machines complete a cycle every 18 minutes (2×3×3) and 24 minutes (2×2×2×3). When will they next finish a cycle together, using prime factorization for LCM?
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: Highest powers: 2×2×2 (from 24) and 3×3 (from 18). LCM=2×2×2×3×3=72 minutes.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: A teacher wants the largest equal group size for 36 boys (2×2×3×3) and 48 girls (2×2×2×2×3), using prime factorization for HCF. What is the group size?
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: Common primes: 2×2 (both have at least two 2’s) and one 3. HCF=2×2×3=12.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: A baker needs the LCM of 15 (3×5) and 25 (5×5) to plan a recipe schedule. What is the LCM using prime factorization?
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: Highest powers: one 3 (from 15) and 5×5 (from 25, since it needs two 5’s). LCM=3×5×5=75.

Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.q: Arrange the steps to find the LCM of 9 (3×3) and 12 (2×2×3) using prime factorization:
Finding HCF & LCM by Prime Factorization.explain: Break both into primes, take the highest power of each prime appearing, then multiply: LCM=36.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: What does a point represent?
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: A point marks an exact location and has no length, width, or size.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: How is a point usually named?
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: Points are named using capital letters like A, B, C.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: Does a line have any endpoints? (type yes or no)
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: A line extends endlessly in both directions and has no endpoints.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: Which of these has a fixed, measurable length?
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: A line segment has two fixed endpoints, giving it a definite length, unlike a line which goes on forever.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: What do we call the two fixed points at the ends of a line segment?
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: The two fixed points marking the ends of a line segment are called its endpoints.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: A perfectly straight road that never ends in either direction is most like a:
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: A line extends endlessly in both directions, just like an unending straight road.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: A pencil or a ruler’s edge is best represented by a:
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: A pencil has two clear ends and a fixed length, making it like a line segment.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: How many endpoints does a line segment have?
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: A line segment has exactly two fixed endpoints.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: Which statement about a point is TRUE?
opts: A point has length but no width
A point has no length, width, or size
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: A point only marks a location — it has no length, width, or size at all.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: Arrange these from smallest defined length to largest (infinite):
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: A point has no length (zero), a line segment has a fixed measurable length, and a line is infinitely long.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: Line segment AB is also known as segment AB or segment ___?
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: A line segment can be named in either order of its endpoints: AB or BA refer to the same segment.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: Why can’t we measure the length of a full line?
opts: Because it extends endlessly in both directions
Because it has no points on it
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: Since a line never ends in either direction, it has no fixed length to measure.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: Three points that lie on the same line are called ___ points.
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: Points lying on the same straight line are called collinear points.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: Which of the following is an example of a line segment in real life?
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: A book’s edge has two fixed ends and a measurable length, making it like a line segment.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: If two points do not lie on the same straight line as a third point, they are called:
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: Points that do not all lie on one line are called non-collinear points.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: A surveyor marks three pegs in a straight row on a field. What term describes these three points?
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: Points lying in a straight row are collinear points.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: A piece of string is cut to exactly 12cm and laid flat with both ends marked. What geometric idea does this represent?
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: The string has two fixed ends and a definite length, just like a line segment.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: A laser pointer’s dot on a wall represents which geometric idea?
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: The dot marks an exact location with no size of its own, just like a point.

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: An architect draws a guideline that is meant to extend infinitely in both directions on a blueprint. What should they draw?
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: Since it extends endlessly in both directions, it should be drawn as a line (with arrows on both ends).

Points, Lines & Line Segments.q: A teacher explains geometry building blocks. Arrange them from most basic to most complex:
Points, Lines & Line Segments.explain: A point is the most basic idea, a line builds on points and extends endlessly, and a line segment is a measured portion between two fixed points.

Rays.q: How many endpoints does a ray have?
Rays.explain: A ray has exactly one endpoint — its starting point — and continues endlessly in the other direction.

Rays.q: Which of these is a good real-life example of a ray?
Rays.explain: A torch beam starts at the torch (one fixed point) and travels onward in one direction, just like a ray.

Rays.q: In ray AB, which point is the starting point?
Rays.explain: When naming a ray, the first letter given is always the starting point.

Rays.q: Are ray AB and ray BA the same ray?
opts: No, they point in opposite directions
Only if A and B are the same point
Rays.explain: Ray AB starts at A and goes through B onward, while ray BA starts at B and goes through A onward — opposite directions.

Rays.q: Which of these has NO endpoints at all?
Rays.explain: A line has no endpoints on either side, unlike a ray (one endpoint) or a line segment (two endpoints).

Rays.q: Does a ray have a fixed, measurable length? (type yes or no)
Rays.explain: Since a ray extends endlessly in one direction, it has no fixed length.

Rays.q: Sun rays reaching the Earth are best modeled as:
Rays.explain: Sunlight starts at the sun (a fixed point) and travels onward in one direction, like a ray.

Rays.q: How does a ray differ from a line segment?
opts: A ray has two endpoints, a segment has one
A ray has one endpoint and goes on forever; a segment has two fixed endpoints
Rays.explain: A ray has one fixed endpoint and extends endlessly, while a line segment has two fixed endpoints and a definite length.

Rays.q: Ray OP starts at point ___?
Rays.explain: The first letter in a ray’s name is always its starting point.

Rays.q: Arrange these by number of endpoints, from most to fewest:
Rays.explain: A line segment has 2 endpoints, a ray has 1, and a line has 0.

Rays.q: When naming a ray, which point is mentioned FIRST?
opts: The endpoint that is farthest away
Rays.explain: The starting point of a ray is always named first.

Rays.q: How many directions does a ray extend in endlessly?
Rays.explain: A ray extends endlessly in only one direction from its starting point.

Rays.q: A car’s headlight shines forward starting from the car and continuing into the distance. This is best modeled as a:
Rays.explain: The light starts at a fixed point (the headlight) and travels onward in one direction, like a ray.

Rays.q: A lighthouse beam sweeps outward from a fixed tower into the sea. What geometric shape best represents the beam at any instant?
Rays.explain: The beam starts at the lighthouse (a fixed point) and extends outward in one direction.

Rays.q: A standing lamp’s light shines upward from its base and continues endlessly upward. This represents a ___?
Rays.explain: The light starts at a fixed point (the lamp) and travels onward in one direction — a ray.

Rays.q: A student draws an arrow on paper starting at point X and passing through point Y, continuing beyond Y. How should this be named?
Rays.explain: Since the arrow starts at X and passes through Y, it should be named ray XY (starting point first).

Rays.q: A spotlight at a concert starts at the stage and shines toward the sky, continuing without limit. Which of the following is true?
opts: It has no endpoints at all
Rays.explain: The spotlight starts at one fixed point (the stage) and extends endlessly in one direction — it has exactly 1 endpoint.

Rays.q: If ray MN and ray NM are drawn on the same two points M and N, do they point in the same direction? (type yes or no)
Rays.explain: Ray MN starts at M and goes through N, while ray NM starts at N and goes through M — opposite directions.

Rays.q: A diagram shows an arrow with one end marked with a dot and the other end with an arrowhead pointing outward forever. What does this represent?
Rays.explain: A dot at one end (the fixed starting point) and an arrowhead showing endless extension represents a ray.

Rays.q: A teacher draws three diagrams: one with 0 endpoints, one with 1 endpoint, one with 2 endpoints. Arrange the matching shapes in that order:
Rays.explain: Line has 0 endpoints, ray has 1, and line segment has 2 — matching the order given.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: What is a point of intersection?
opts: Where two lines cross each other
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: The point of intersection is where two lines cross or meet.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: How many points of intersection do two distinct straight lines have at most?
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: Two distinct straight lines can cross at most at one single point.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: Do parallel lines ever meet, no matter how far they are extended? (type yes or no)
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: Parallel lines never meet, no matter how far they are extended.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: Which of these is a good real-life example of parallel lines?
opts: The two rails of a railway track
Two roads crossing at a junction
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: The two rails of a railway track always stay the same distance apart and never meet — they are parallel.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: Which of these is a good real-life example of intersecting lines?
opts: The two long sides of a door
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: The plus sign shows two lines crossing at a single central point — intersecting lines.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: What is the distance between two parallel lines — does it stay the same or change?
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: Parallel lines always remain the same distance apart from each other.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: If two lines cross at exactly one point, what are they called?
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: Lines that cross at one point are called intersecting lines (perpendicular lines are a special case of intersecting lines that cross at a right angle).

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: The two diagonals of a square are:
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: The diagonals of a square cross each other at the center, making them intersecting lines.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: The opposite sides of a rectangle are an example of what kind of lines?
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: Opposite sides of a rectangle never meet and stay the same distance apart — they are parallel.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: Can three or more lines all intersect at the very same point?
opts: No, only two lines can ever intersect
Yes, this is possible and such lines are called concurrent lines
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: When three or more lines pass through a single common point, they are called concurrent lines.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: Arrange in the order: intersecting, then parallel, based on whether the lines meet:
items: Lines that cross at one point
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: Intersecting lines cross at a point; parallel lines never meet — matching the requested order.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: Two rows of bricks built one above the other, always staying the same distance apart, are an example of ___ lines.
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: Since the rows never get closer or farther apart, they are parallel.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: A road map shows two streets that cross each other at a traffic signal. These streets are:
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: Since the streets cross at the traffic signal, they are intersecting lines.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: A ladder is placed against a wall, and its two side rails never get closer or farther apart as they go up. These rails are:
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: Since the rails stay the same distance apart throughout, they are parallel.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: Two scissor blades are joined at a pivot and can swing to cross each other. At the pivot point, what relationship do the blades have?
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: The blades cross at the pivot point, making them intersecting lines at that point.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: A football field has two sidelines running the full length of the field, always staying the same distance apart. These sidelines are:
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: Since they remain equally spaced throughout the field’s length, the sidelines are parallel.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: On a map, two highways are shown crossing each other once before continuing in different directions. What can you conclude?
opts: They are intersecting lines, with one point of intersection
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: Since they cross exactly once, they are intersecting lines, with that crossing point being their point of intersection.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: A fence is built with each post connected by two horizontal rails that never touch each other along their length. These rails are ___?
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: Since the rails never touch and stay equally spaced, they are parallel.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: Three roads in a town all pass through the same central roundabout. What are these three roads called?
opts: Concurrent (lines all crossing at one point)
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: Since all three roads pass through the same single point (the roundabout), they are concurrent lines.

Intersecting & Parallel Lines.q: A city planner explains line relationships using roads. Arrange these examples from “never meet” to “cross at multiple different points” (note: distinct straight lines cross at most once, so the third example must use curved roads):
items: Two parallel avenues running side by side
Two roads crossing once at an intersection
Two winding roads crossing at several different points
Intersecting & Parallel Lines.explain: Parallel lines never meet, straight intersecting lines cross exactly once, and only curved paths (not straight lines) can cross more than once.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: In geometry, what counts as a curve?
opts: Any drawing made without lifting the pencil, including straight lines
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: In mathematics, a curve includes any unbroken drawing made without lifting the pencil — even straight lines count.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: What makes a curve “closed”?
opts: It is drawn with a ruler
Its starting and ending points meet, forming a loop
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: A closed curve’s start and end points meet, forming a complete loop with no gaps.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: Is the letter “O” an open or closed curve?
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: The letter O forms a complete loop with no gaps, making it a closed curve.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: Is the letter “U” an open or closed curve?
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: The letter U does not loop back to its starting point, so it is an open curve.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: What is a simple curve?
opts: A curve that does not cross itself
A curve with only straight lines
A curve that is always closed
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: A simple curve does not cross over itself anywhere along its path.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: How many regions does a simple closed curve divide a page into?
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: A simple closed curve creates three regions: the interior, the boundary (the curve itself), and the exterior.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: What is the region INSIDE a simple closed curve called?
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: The inside region of a simple closed curve is called its interior.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: What is the region OUTSIDE a simple closed curve called?
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: The outside region of a simple closed curve is called its exterior.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: A circle is an example of a:
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: A circle’s path joins back to where it started, making it a closed curve.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: A wavy line shaped like the letter “S” (without joining ends) is an example of a:
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: Since the two ends of the S-shape do not meet, it is an open curve.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: Arrange these curve types from “ends never meet” to “ends always meet”:
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: In an open curve, the ends never meet; in a closed curve, the ends always meet — matching the requested order.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: Is a curve that crosses itself considered “simple”? (type yes or no)
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: A simple curve must NOT cross itself — if it does, it is not simple.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: A child draws a wavy path on paper without lifting the pencil, and the path eventually returns to its starting dot. What type of curve is this?
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: Since the path returns to its starting point, it forms a loop and is a closed curve.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: A hiking trail map shows a path that starts at the trailhead and ends at a different lookout point, never looping back. What type of curve does this represent?
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: Since the trail’s start and end points are different and don’t meet, it is an open curve.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: A racetrack is shaped so cars return to the same starting line after one full lap. Is this track an open or closed curve?
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: Since the track loops back to the starting point, it is a closed curve.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: A garden is shaped like a closed curve, and a gardener wants to know where to plant flowers “inside” the boundary. Which region should they use?
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: Planting “inside” the garden’s boundary means using the interior region.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: A piece of string is laid on a table in a loop with the two ends touching. Which best describes this shape?
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: Since the ends touch, forming a loop, it is a closed curve.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: A snail’s trail starts at a leaf and ends at a different spot in the garden, never crossing itself or looping back. List one term that describes this curve (open or closed, AND simple or not).
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: Since the trail doesn’t loop back (open) and doesn’t cross itself (simple), it is both an open curve and a simple curve.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: An artist draws a figure-8 shape, which crosses over itself once in the middle. Is this a simple curve?
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: Since the figure-8 crosses itself, it is NOT a simple curve.

Curves — Open & Closed.q: A teacher shows three shapes: a circle, a letter “C”, and a figure-8. Arrange them as: simple closed, open, not simple.
Curves — Open & Closed.explain: A circle is simple and closed, the letter C is open (and simple), and a figure-8 crosses itself so it is not simple — matching the requested order.

Polygons.q: What is a polygon made of?
opts: A mix of curves and points
Polygons.explain: A polygon is a simple closed curve made entirely of straight line segments.

Polygons.q: Why is a circle NOT a polygon?
opts: It is made of a curve, not straight line segments
Polygons.explain: Polygons must be made of straight line segments; a circle is curved, so it cannot be a polygon.

Polygons.q: What do we call the line segments that make up a polygon?
Polygons.explain: The straight line segments forming a polygon are called its sides.

Polygons.q: What do we call the point where two sides of a polygon meet?
Polygons.explain: The meeting point of two sides of a polygon is called a vertex (plural: vertices).

Polygons.q: What is the name for two sides that share a common vertex?
Polygons.explain: Two sides sharing a common vertex are called adjacent sides.

Polygons.q: A polygon with 5 sides is called a:
Polygons.explain: A 5-sided polygon is called a pentagon.

Polygons.q: A polygon with 6 sides is called a:
Polygons.explain: A 6-sided polygon is called a hexagon.

Polygons.q: How many vertices does an octagon (8-sided polygon) have?
Polygons.explain: A polygon always has the same number of vertices as it has sides — so an octagon has 8 vertices.

Polygons.q: What is the minimum number of sides a polygon can have?
Polygons.explain: A polygon needs at least 3 sides — fewer than 3 line segments cannot enclose a region.

Polygons.q: In a polygon, the number of angles always equals the number of ___?
Polygons.explain: A polygon’s number of angles, vertices, and sides are always equal to each other.

Polygons.q: Arrange these polygons from fewest to most sides:
Polygons.explain: Triangle (3 sides), Pentagon (5 sides), Hexagon (6 sides) — from fewest to most.

Polygons.q: A stop sign with 8 equal sides is an example of a:
Polygons.explain: An 8-sided shape is called an octagon, matching a typical stop sign.

Polygons.q: A honeycomb cell has 6 straight sides. What type of polygon is each cell?
Polygons.explain: A 6-sided shape is a hexagon, matching the honeycomb cell.

Polygons.q: A garden bed is designed with 4 straight sides and 4 corners. What is the minimum classification for this shape?
Polygons.explain: A 4-sided polygon is classified as a quadrilateral.

Polygons.q: A sign has 3 straight sides and 3 corners. What is this shape called?
Polygons.explain: A 3-sided polygon is called a triangle.

Polygons.q: An architect designs a window with 5 straight edges and 5 corners. Two of the edges meet at a single point. What do we call that meeting point?
Polygons.explain: The point where two sides meet is called a vertex.

Polygons.q: A floor tile is shaped with 7 straight sides. What is this polygon called?
Polygons.explain: A 7-sided polygon is called a heptagon.

Polygons.q: A picture frame has 4 sides, where each pair of neighboring sides meets at a corner. Name one pair of adjacent sides if the frame is ABCD (use two side names, e.g. AB and BC).
Polygons.explain: Sides AB and BC share vertex B, making them adjacent sides (other valid answers: BC and CD, CD and DA, DA and AB).

Polygons.q: A kite-shaped sign has 4 sides total. How many vertices and how many angles does it have?
Polygons.explain: Since it is a 4-sided polygon, it has 4 vertices and 4 angles, matching the number of sides.

Polygons.q: A teacher asks students to name polygons by side count in increasing order:
Polygons.explain: Quadrilateral has 4 sides, Pentagon has 5, Hexagon has 6 — increasing order.

Angles & Their Parts.q: An angle is formed by two:
opts: Rays sharing a common starting point
Angles & Their Parts.explain: An angle is formed when two rays share the same starting point (the vertex).

Angles & Their Parts.q: What is the common starting point of an angle called?
Angles & Their Parts.explain: The shared starting point of the two rays forming an angle is called the vertex.

Angles & Their Parts.q: What are the two rays forming an angle called?
Angles & Their Parts.explain: The two rays forming an angle are called its arms (or sides).

Angles & Their Parts.q: In angle ∠XYZ, which letter is the vertex?
Angles & Their Parts.explain: The middle letter in an angle’s name always represents the vertex — here, Y.

Angles & Their Parts.q: When naming an angle with 3 letters, which position does the vertex go in?
Angles & Their Parts.explain: The vertex is always written as the middle letter when naming an angle with three letters.

Angles & Their Parts.q: How many regions does an angle divide a plane into (besides the angle itself)?
Angles & Their Parts.explain: An angle creates two additional regions: the interior (between the arms) and the exterior (everything else).

Angles & Their Parts.q: What is the region BETWEEN the two arms of an angle called?
Angles & Their Parts.explain: The region between the arms of an angle is called its interior.

Angles & Their Parts.q: If two angles share the same vertex AND one common ray, what do they have in common?
opts: Only a ray, not the vertex
One common ray and one common point (the vertex)
Angles & Their Parts.explain: If two angles share a ray, that ray’s starting point (the vertex) is also automatically shared.

Angles & Their Parts.q: A point lying exactly on one of the arms of an angle is:
Angles & Their Parts.explain: Points on either arm are part of the angle itself, not the interior or exterior.

Angles & Their Parts.q: Arrange the parts of naming angle ∠ABC in the order they appear (first letter, vertex, last letter):
Angles & Their Parts.explain: In ∠ABC, A comes first, B is the vertex (middle), and C comes last.

Angles & Their Parts.q: How many rays are needed to form a single angle?
Angles & Their Parts.explain: An angle is formed by exactly two rays sharing a common starting point.

Angles & Their Parts.q: Rays OP and OQ together form which angle (assuming O is the shared vertex)?
Angles & Their Parts.explain: The angle is named ∠POQ (or equivalently ∠QOP) with O as the vertex in the middle.

Angles & Their Parts.q: An open book forms an angle at its spine. What part of the angle does the spine represent?
Angles & Their Parts.explain: The spine is the common point where the two halves (arms) of the book meet — the vertex.

Angles & Their Parts.q: A pair of scissors is opened, forming an angle at the pivot. What do the two blades represent?
Angles & Their Parts.explain: The two blades are the rays of the angle, making them its arms.

Angles & Their Parts.q: A clock’s hands form an angle at the center. What part of the angle does the center of the clock represent?
Angles & Their Parts.explain: The center of the clock is the shared starting point of both hands — the vertex.

Angles & Their Parts.q: A carpenter measures the angle of a door as it swings open. Which two parts of the door form the arms of the angle?
opts: The door and the door frame edge it swings from
The door handle and the lock
Angles & Their Parts.explain: The door (one arm) and the fixed frame edge (other arm) meeting at the hinge (vertex) form the angle.

Angles & Their Parts.q: A surveyor marks two rays from a common point to measure land boundaries. What is this common point called in geometry?
Angles & Their Parts.explain: The shared starting point of the two rays is called the vertex.

Angles & Their Parts.q: A student draws ∠MNP. Which letter must be the vertex?
Angles & Their Parts.explain: The middle letter in the angle’s name is always the vertex — here, N.

Angles & Their Parts.q: A kite has two strings forming an angle where they attach to the frame. A point resting exactly on one of the strings is:
opts: In the interior of the angle
In the exterior of the angle
Angles & Their Parts.explain: A point on either of the strings (arms) is considered part of the angle itself.

Angles & Their Parts.q: A teacher describes how an angle divides a page. Arrange the regions from “closest to the vertex” outward: the angle itself, interior, exterior (treating exterior as farthest):
Angles & Their Parts.explain: The arms form the angle itself, the interior lies between them, and the exterior is everything beyond — in that outward order.

Triangles.q: How many sides does a triangle have?
Triangles.explain: A triangle always has exactly 3 sides.

Triangles.q: How many vertices does a triangle have?
Triangles.explain: A triangle always has exactly 3 vertices.

Triangles.q: How many angles does every triangle have?
Triangles.explain: A triangle always has exactly 3 angles, one at each vertex.

Triangles.q: A triangle with vertices A, B, C is written as:
Triangles.explain: A triangle with vertices A, B, C is written as triangle ABC or using the symbol △ABC.

Triangles.q: What is the polygon with the FEWEST possible number of sides?
Triangles.explain: A triangle, with 3 sides, is the polygon with the fewest possible sides.

Triangles.q: In triangle PQR, what are its three sides?
Triangles.explain: The three sides of triangle PQR are PQ, QR, and RP — connecting each pair of vertices.

Triangles.q: Why are triangles often used in bridges and roof structures?
opts: They are very stable and resist bending
Triangles.explain: Triangles are extremely stable and don’t bend out of shape easily, making them ideal for construction.

Triangles.q: A point exactly inside a triangle’s boundary lies in its ___?
Triangles.explain: A point inside the triangle’s edges lies in its interior region.

Triangles.q: A point far outside a triangle’s edges lies in its:
Triangles.explain: A point outside the triangle’s edges lies in its exterior region.

Triangles.q: Arrange in order: vertices, sides, angles — by typical reading order when describing a triangle (vertices first, since they define the shape; then the sides connecting them; then the angles formed):
Triangles.explain: We usually first name the vertices, then the sides connecting them, and lastly the angles they form.

Triangles.q: Triangle ABC has angles ∠BAC, ∠ABC, and which third angle?
Triangles.explain: The third angle of triangle ABC, at vertex C, is ∠BCA (or equivalently ∠ACB).

Triangles.q: Is a triangle a type of polygon?
Triangles.explain: A triangle is indeed a polygon — in fact, the simplest one, with the fewest sides.

Triangles.q: A slice of pizza, cut from the center to the crust on two sides, forms roughly which shape?
Triangles.explain: The slice has 3 straight-ish edges meeting at 3 points, resembling a triangle.

Triangles.q: A bicycle frame uses a triangular shape for the main structure. Why might engineers choose this shape?
opts: Triangles are the most stable polygon shape, resisting bending
Triangles are the easiest to paint
Triangles.explain: Triangles are very rigid and resist bending under pressure, which is why they’re used in strong structures.

Triangles.q: A yield traffic sign is shaped with 3 equal sides. What is this shape called?
Triangles.explain: A shape with 3 sides is a triangle, matching the typical yield sign.

Triangles.q: A roof truss is built using triangle shapes. If one truss is named △XYZ, how many vertices does it have?
Triangles.explain: Since it is a triangle, it has exactly 3 vertices: X, Y, and Z.

Triangles.q: A sailboat’s sail is shaped like a triangle. A bird perches exactly on one edge of the sail. Where is the bird located relative to the triangle?
opts: On the triangle itself (on a side)
Triangles.explain: Since the bird is on an edge (a side), it is on the triangle itself, not strictly interior or exterior.

Triangles.q: A warning sign uses a triangle shape with vertices labeled D, E, F. Name all three sides of this triangle.
Triangles.explain: The three sides connecting the vertices of triangle DEF are DE, EF, and FD.

Triangles.q: An artist paints a triangular flag with vertices P, Q, R. A dot is painted exactly at the center of the flag. Where is this dot located?
Triangles.explain: A point at the center of the triangle, not on any edge, lies in the interior.

Triangles.q: A construction worker explains why triangles are used in towers. Arrange the reasoning in logical order:
items: This is why triangle shapes are common in towers and bridges
Triangles do not easily change shape under force, unlike squares
A triangle’s fixed side lengths keep its angles fixed too
Triangles.explain: Fixed side lengths fix the angles, which makes triangles resist bending, which is why they’re used in construction — in that logical order.

Quadrilaterals.q: How many sides does a quadrilateral have?
Quadrilaterals.explain: A quadrilateral always has exactly 4 sides.

Quadrilaterals.q: How many vertices and angles does a quadrilateral have?
Quadrilaterals.explain: A quadrilateral has 4 vertices and 4 angles, matching its 4 sides.

Quadrilaterals.q: In quadrilateral ABCD, which side is opposite to side AB?
Quadrilaterals.explain: Side CD does not share a vertex with AB, making it the opposite side.

Quadrilaterals.q: In quadrilateral ABCD, which angle is opposite to angle A?
Quadrilaterals.explain: Angle C is the opposite angle to angle A in quadrilateral ABCD.

Quadrilaterals.q: What is a diagonal of a quadrilateral?
opts: A line segment joining two opposite vertices
Quadrilaterals.explain: A diagonal connects two vertices that are not next to each other (opposite vertices).

Quadrilaterals.q: How many diagonals does a quadrilateral have?
Quadrilaterals.explain: A quadrilateral has exactly 2 diagonals, connecting each pair of opposite vertices.

Quadrilaterals.q: In quadrilateral PQRS, name its two diagonals.
Quadrilaterals.explain: The diagonals connect opposite vertices: P to R, and Q to S.

Quadrilaterals.q: Two sides that share a common vertex are called:
Quadrilaterals.explain: Sides sharing a common vertex are called adjacent sides.

Quadrilaterals.q: In quadrilateral WXYZ, are sides WX and XY adjacent or opposite?
opts: Adjacent, since they share vertex X
Quadrilaterals.explain: WX and XY share vertex X, making them adjacent sides.

Quadrilaterals.q: Arrange the steps to correctly name a quadrilateral with 4 given vertices:
items: Write the four vertex letters in this cyclic order
Make sure each consecutive pair of letters forms an actual side (going around the shape, not skipping across)
Identify the 4 vertices in order around the shape
Quadrilaterals.explain: First identify the vertices in order around the shape, ensure consecutive letters form real sides, then write the name in that cyclic order.

Quadrilaterals.q: A quadrilateral ABCD has how many pairs of opposite sides?
Quadrilaterals.explain: A quadrilateral has 2 pairs of opposite sides: AB & CD, and BC & DA.

Quadrilaterals.q: A quadrilateral ABCD has how many pairs of opposite angles?
Quadrilaterals.explain: A quadrilateral has 2 pairs of opposite angles: ∠A & ∠C, and ∠B & ∠D.

Quadrilaterals.q: A kite-shaped toy has 4 vertices labeled K, I, T, E in order. What are its diagonals?
Quadrilaterals.explain: Diagonals connect opposite vertices: K to T, and I to E.

Quadrilaterals.q: A rectangular picture frame has corners A, B, C, D in order. Which sides are adjacent to side AB?
Quadrilaterals.explain: Side AB shares vertex A with side DA, and shares vertex B with side BC — both are adjacent to AB.

Quadrilaterals.q: A four-sided garden plot has corners labeled G, A, R, D in order. Name one diagonal of this plot.
Quadrilaterals.explain: GR connects opposite vertices G and R (the other diagonal is AD).

Quadrilaterals.q: A door is shaped as quadrilateral WXYZ. If a carpenter wants to reinforce it by adding a diagonal brace, which of these is a valid diagonal?
Quadrilaterals.explain: WY connects opposite (non-adjacent) vertices W and Y, making it a valid diagonal (WX and XY are sides, not diagonals).

Quadrilaterals.q: A tile is shaped like quadrilateral PQRS. A line is drawn from P to R, splitting the tile into two triangles. What is this line called?
Quadrilaterals.explain: A line connecting opposite vertices (P and R) inside a quadrilateral is called a diagonal.

Quadrilaterals.q: A quadrilateral-shaped sign has vertices labeled 1, 2, 3, 4 in order. Name the side opposite to side formed by vertices 2 and 3.
Quadrilaterals.answer: the side formed by vertices 4 and 1
Quadrilaterals.explain: Side 2-3 is opposite to side 4-1, since neither pair shares a vertex with the other.

Quadrilaterals.q: A book cover is shaped like quadrilateral MNOP. Which pair of angles are opposite to each other?
opts: All four angles are opposite to each other
Quadrilaterals.explain: In quadrilateral MNOP, ∠M is opposite ∠O, and ∠N is opposite ∠P.

Quadrilaterals.q: A teacher explains quadrilateral parts. Arrange these from “simplest part” to “most complex relationship”: side, vertex, diagonal.
items: Side (a segment connecting two adjacent vertices)
Quadrilaterals.explain: A vertex is a single point, a side connects two adjacent vertices, and a diagonal connects two non-adjacent (opposite) vertices — increasing in complexity.

Circles.q: What is a circle?
opts: A simple closed curve where all points are the same distance from a center
Circles.explain: A circle is a simple closed curve made of points all the same distance from a fixed center point.

Circles.q: Why is a circle NOT a polygon?
opts: It has no straight sides at all
Circles.explain: A polygon needs straight sides, but a circle is made of a curve with no straight sides.

Circles.q: What is the line segment joining the centre of a circle to any point on the circle called?
Circles.explain: The radius connects the centre to any point on the circle’s edge.

Circles.q: What is the line segment passing through the centre, connecting two opposite points on the circle, called?
Circles.explain: The diameter passes through the centre and connects two points on opposite sides of the circle.

Circles.q: The diameter of a circle is always:
Circles.explain: The diameter is always twice the length of the radius (d=2r).

Circles.q: If a circle has a radius of 6cm, what is its diameter?
Circles.explain: Diameter = 2 × radius = 2×6=12cm.

Circles.q: If a circle has a diameter of 20cm, what is its radius?
Circles.explain: Radius = diameter ÷ 2 = 20÷2=10cm.

Circles.q: What is a chord of a circle?
opts: Any line segment joining two points on the circle
Circles.explain: A chord is any line segment joining two points on the circle’s edge (the diameter is the longest possible chord).

Circles.q: Is the diameter considered a chord?
opts: No, it is different from a chord
Yes, it is the longest possible chord
Circles.explain: The diameter is a special chord — the longest one possible, since it passes through the centre.

Circles.q: What is an arc of a circle?
opts: A part of the circle’s boundary (curved edge)
A straight line through the circle
Circles.explain: An arc is a portion of the circle’s curved boundary.

Circles.q: What do we call a “pizza slice” shaped region between two radii and an arc?
Circles.explain: This pizza-slice-shaped region is called a sector.

Circles.q: What is a segment of a circle?
opts: The region between a chord and its arc
Circles.explain: A segment is the region between a chord and the arc it cuts off (different from a sector, which uses two radii).

Circles.q: Arrange these from shortest to longest, given a circle of radius 5cm: a chord of length 6cm, the radius, the diameter.
Circles.explain: Radius=5cm, the given chord=6cm, and diameter=10cm — from shortest to longest.

Circles.q: A wheel has a radius of 14cm. What is its diameter?
Circles.explain: Diameter = 2 × radius = 2×14=28cm.

Circles.q: A circular table has a diameter of 90cm. What is its radius?
Circles.explain: Radius = diameter ÷ 2 = 90÷2=45cm.

Circles.q: A pizza is cut into slices from the center to the crust. What is the name for each pizza slice shape in geometry?
Circles.explain: Each pizza slice, bounded by two radii and an arc of crust, is called a sector.

Circles.q: A coin has a radius of 1.2cm. What is its diameter?
Circles.explain: Diameter = 2 × radius = 2×1.2=2.4cm.

Circles.q: A circular cake is sliced once straight across (not through the center), separating a small piece from the rest. What 2 geometric terms describe the cut and the small piece?
Circles.explain: The straight cut not through the centre is a chord, and the resulting small piece (between the chord and its arc) is a segment.

Circles.q: A circular running track has a diameter of 100m. What is the radius of the track?
Circles.explain: Radius = diameter ÷ 2 = 100÷2=50m.

Circles.q: A teacher explains circle parts using a clock. Arrange in the order: the part connecting center to edge, the part connecting two edge points through the center, the curved edge itself.
Circles.explain: Radius connects center to edge, diameter connects edge to edge through the center, and the arc is the curved boundary itself — matching the requested order.

Measuring Line Segments.q: What makes a line segment different from a line?
opts: It has two fixed endpoints and a definite length
Measuring Line Segments.explain: A line segment has two fixed endpoints, giving it a definite, measurable length; a line extends forever in both directions.

Measuring Line Segments.q: Which method of comparing line segments is the LEAST accurate?
opts: By tracing one onto the other
Measuring Line Segments.explain: Observation alone can be fooled when two segments are close in length — it is the least accurate method.

Measuring Line Segments.q: A line segment starts at the 2cm mark and ends at the 9cm mark on a ruler. How long is it (in cm)?
Measuring Line Segments.explain: Length = ending mark − starting mark = 9 − 2 = 7cm.

Measuring Line Segments.q: What should you do to find the length of a segment using a ruler?
opts: Subtract the smaller reading from the larger reading
Measuring Line Segments.explain: Always subtract the smaller reading from the larger reading to get the correct length.

Measuring Line Segments.q: What tool has two pointed, adjustable legs and gives a more accurate measurement than a ruler alone?
Measuring Line Segments.explain: A divider has two adjustable pointed legs used to copy a length exactly for accurate measurement.

Measuring Line Segments.q: A line segment runs from the 5cm mark to the 13cm mark. What is its length (in cm)?
Why might reading a ruler directly give a slightly wrong answer sometimes?
opts: Looking at the ruler from an angle (angle of vision) can cause small errors
Measuring Line Segments.explain: Viewing the ruler from an angle instead of straight-on can cause a small reading error — a divider avoids this.

Measuring Line Segments.q: Which of these is the correct way to use a divider to measure a segment?
opts: Open it to match the two endpoints, then place it on a ruler without changing the opening
Open it as wide as possible, then guess the length
Use only one leg of the divider, ignoring the other
Measuring Line Segments.explain: You open the divider exactly to match the endpoints, then transfer that exact opening onto a ruler to read the length.

Measuring Line Segments.q: A segment is measured from the 0cm mark to the 11cm mark. What is its length (in cm)?
Comparing two pencils just by looking at them works well when:
opts: Their lengths are clearly very different
Measuring Line Segments.explain: Observation alone is reliable only when the difference in length is large and obvious.

Measuring Line Segments.q: Arrange these segment lengths from SHORTEST to LONGEST: a 4cm segment, a 9cm segment, a 1cm segment.
Measuring Line Segments.explain: 1cm → 4cm → 9cm, from shortest to longest.

Measuring Line Segments.q: A line segment has endpoints A and B. What is another common way to write this segment?
opts: Segment AB or just AB with a bar on top
Measuring Line Segments.explain: A line segment between points A and B is written as segment AB, often with a bar symbol on top.

Measuring Line Segments.q: A segment measured from 3.5cm to 10.5cm on a ruler is how long (in cm)?
Rohan wants to check if his pencil is longer than his eraser just by glancing at them on the table. Which comparison method is he using?
Measuring Line Segments.explain: Glancing and judging by eye, without tools, is comparison by observation.

Measuring Line Segments.q: A tailor needs to cut cloth to an EXACT length and cannot afford even a small error. Which tool should they trust most for precision?
opts: A divider used carefully with a ruler
Just folding the cloth in half
Measuring Line Segments.explain: A divider used with a ruler gives the most accurate, error-free measurement for precise work.

Measuring Line Segments.q: A ribbon is placed along a ruler. It starts at the 1cm mark and ends at the 14cm mark. How long is the ribbon (in cm)?
Meera traces one string exactly on top of another string to see which one is longer. What comparison method is this?
Measuring Line Segments.explain: Placing one object exactly on top of another to compare lengths is the tracing method.

Measuring Line Segments.q: If a segment measures 7cm using one ruler reading, and the SAME segment measures 7.1cm with a divider transferred carefully — which is likely more accurate?
opts: The divider-based reading, since it avoids angle-of-vision error
Measuring Line Segments.explain: A divider transferred to a ruler avoids angle-of-vision error, making it generally more accurate than a direct ruler reading.

Measuring Line Segments.q: A wire is cut and measured against a ruler. It starts at the 6cm mark and ends at the 20cm mark. How long is the wire (in cm)?
A student measures three pieces of string: String A from 0–5cm, String B from 0–12cm, String C from 0–8cm. Arrange the strings from SHORTEST to LONGEST.
Measuring Line Segments.explain: String A=5cm, String C=8cm, String B=12cm — shortest to longest.

Angles & Their Types.q: An angle is formed when two rays meet at a:
Angles & Their Types.explain: An angle is formed by two rays sharing a common endpoint, called the vertex.

Angles & Their Types.q: What do we call the two rays that form an angle?
Angles & Their Types.explain: The two rays of an angle are called its arms.

Angles & Their Types.q: A right angle measures exactly:
Angles & Their Types.explain: A right angle measures exactly 90° — like a perfect corner.

Angles & Their Types.q: A straight angle measures exactly:
Angles & Their Types.explain: A straight angle measures exactly 180°, with arms pointing in opposite directions.

Angles & Their Types.q: A complete angle (full turn) measures how many degrees?
Angles & Their Types.explain: A complete angle, or full turn, measures 360°.

Angles & Their Types.q: An angle measuring 40° is called:
Angles & Their Types.explain: An angle smaller than 90° is an acute angle.

Angles & Their Types.q: An angle measuring 150° is called:
Angles & Their Types.explain: An angle bigger than 90° but smaller than 180° is an obtuse angle.

Angles & Their Types.q: An angle measuring 250° is called:
Angles & Their Types.explain: An angle bigger than 180° but smaller than 360° is a reflex angle.

Angles & Their Types.q: How many right angles make up a straight angle?
Angles & Their Types.explain: 180° ÷ 90° = 2 right angles make a straight angle.

Angles & Their Types.q: Which range of degrees describes an acute angle?
Angles & Their Types.explain: An acute angle is any angle between 0° and 90° (not including either).

Angles & Their Types.q: Which range of degrees describes an obtuse angle?
Angles & Their Types.explain: An obtuse angle is between 90° and 180° (not including either).

Angles & Their Types.q: What is the name of the angle that measures more than 180° but less than 360°?
Angles & Their Types.explain: An angle between 180° and 360° is called a reflex angle.

Angles & Their Types.q: How many right angles make up a complete angle (360°)?
Angles & Their Types.explain: 360° ÷ 90° = 4 right angles make a complete angle.

Angles & Their Types.q: Arrange these angle types from SMALLEST measure to LARGEST: obtuse, acute, reflex.
Angles & Their Types.explain: Acute (<90°) → Obtuse (90°–180°) → Reflex (180°–360°), smallest to largest.

Angles & Their Types.q: A book lies open flat on a table, its two covers forming a straight line. What angle do the covers form?
Angles & Their Types.explain: When the covers form a straight line, the angle between them is a straight angle (180°).

Angles & Their Types.q: A door is opened just slightly, making a narrow angle with the door frame. What type of angle is this most likely?
Angles & Their Types.explain: A door opened just slightly forms a small, narrow angle — an acute angle (less than 90°).

Angles & Their Types.q: A laptop screen is opened wide, beyond a right angle but not flat. What is this angle type? (one word)
Angles & Their Types.explain: An angle bigger than 90° but smaller than 180° is obtuse — a wide-open laptop screen is a good example.

Angles & Their Types.q: The corner of a square picture frame forms what type of angle?
Angles & Their Types.explain: The corner of a square or rectangle is always a right angle (90°).

Angles & Their Types.q: A clock’s hands point at 12 and 6, forming a straight line between them. Going one direction it is 180°. What is the angle if measured going the OTHER (longer) way around?
opts: It would be a reflex angle, more than 180°
Angles & Their Types.explain: Since 12 and 6 are exactly opposite, BOTH directions measure 180° — splitting the full 360° circle exactly in half.

Angles & Their Types.q: A fan blade sweeps through more than half a full turn but less than a complete turn. What type of angle does this describe? (one word)
Angles & Their Types.explain: An angle greater than 180° (more than half a turn) but less than 360° is a reflex angle.

Measuring Angles.q: What tool is used to measure angles accurately?
Measuring Angles.explain: A protractor, marked from 0° to 180°, is the tool used to accurately measure angles.

Measuring Angles.q: What is the FIRST step when measuring an angle with a protractor?
opts: Place the centre point of the protractor exactly on the vertex
Measuring Angles.explain: You must first align the protractor’s centre point with the angle’s vertex before reading any measurement.

Measuring Angles.q: A protractor is shaped like a half-circle and is marked from 0° to how many degrees?
Measuring Angles.explain: A standard protractor’s scale runs from 0° to 180°.

Measuring Angles.q: Why do protractors usually have TWO rows of numbers?
opts: Because the scales run in opposite directions, for measuring from either side
Because one row is always wrong
Measuring Angles.explain: The two scales run in opposite directions (0°→180° and 180°→0°) so you can measure from whichever side the angle opens.

Measuring Angles.q: If you align the base line with the LEFT 0° mark, which scale should you read?
opts: The one starting at 0° on the left
The one starting at 0° on the right
Measuring Angles.explain: Always read the scale that matches the 0° mark you used as your starting reference.

Measuring Angles.q: What part of the angle must be placed exactly at the centre point of the protractor?
Measuring Angles.explain: The protractor’s centre point must align exactly with the angle’s vertex for an accurate reading.

Measuring Angles.q: After measuring, an arm of the angle crosses the inner scale at 40° (matching your chosen 0°). What is the angle’s measure?
Measuring Angles.explain: Since 40° is read on the matching scale, the angle measures exactly 40°.

Measuring Angles.q: To draw an angle of a given measure, what do you do FIRST?
opts: Mark the degree dot before drawing anything
Draw one ray (arm) of the angle first
Measuring Angles.explain: You start by drawing one ray, then place the protractor along it to mark the required degree.

Measuring Angles.q: After marking the correct degree dot with a protractor, what tool do you use to join the vertex to the dot?
Measuring Angles.explain: A ruler is used to draw a straight line from the vertex through the marked dot, completing the angle.

Measuring Angles.q: A student reads 130° on the scale but actually placed the base line at the opposite 0°. What is their mistake?
opts: They should have read the other scale, since they mixed up the matching 0° mark
Measuring Angles.explain: Reading the wrong scale (not matching your chosen 0° baseline) gives an incorrect angle measure.

Measuring Angles.q: A protractor reading shows the angle exactly at the halfway mark of the scale. What is this angle’s measure?
Measuring Angles.explain: The halfway mark on a 0°–180° protractor scale is 90°.

Measuring Angles.q: If the base line is aligned at the right 0° mark, and the arm crosses at the right-scale’s 70 mark, what is the angle (in degrees)?
Measuring Angles.explain: Since both the base line and the reading use the matching right-side scale, the angle is 70°.

Measuring Angles.q: A carpenter wants to cut a wooden piece at exactly 35°. What tool should they use to mark this precise angle?
Measuring Angles.explain: A protractor is the correct tool for marking a precise angle measure like 35°.

Measuring Angles.q: An architect draws a roof design with a 120° angle at the peak. Which tool would they use to verify this on paper?
Measuring Angles.explain: A protractor is used to measure or verify angle measures like 120° on a drawing.

Measuring Angles.q: A student measures an angle and gets 55° using the correctly matched scale. If they had mistakenly used the other (unmatched) scale, what would the WRONG reading have been? (180 − 55 = ?)
Measuring Angles.explain: Reading the unmatched scale would have given 180° − 55° = 125°, the wrong answer.

Measuring Angles.q: Why is it important to place the protractor’s centre EXACTLY on the vertex, not slightly off?
opts: It doesn’t matter, any nearby point works
A misaligned centre will give an inaccurate angle reading
Protractors only work if centred on paper edges
Measuring Angles.explain: Even a small misalignment of the centre point can shift the reading and produce an inaccurate angle measure.

Measuring Angles.q: A protractor shows an arm crossing both scales at once near a tricky spot. Which scale is correct?
opts: The one matching the 0° you used for your base line
Measuring Angles.explain: Always use the reading from the scale that matches the 0° mark where your base line is aligned.

Measuring Angles.q: An angle is to be drawn at exactly 75°. After placing the protractor and marking the dot at 75°, what should be done next? (one word: the tool used to connect vertex and dot)
Measuring Angles.explain: A ruler is used to draw the straight line from the vertex through the 75° dot, completing the angle.

Measuring Angles.q: A student draws a 50° angle but later checks with a protractor and finds it actually measures 48°. What is the most likely reason for this small error?
opts: The angle changed shape on its own
A slight misalignment of the protractor or ruler while marking/drawing
It is impossible to ever measure 50° accurately
Measuring Angles.explain: Small drawing or alignment errors when using the protractor or ruler often cause slight measurement differences.

Measuring Angles.q: Arrange the steps for measuring an angle with a protractor in the correct order:
items: Read the scale where the other arm crosses
Place the centre point exactly on the vertex
Align the base line with one arm of the angle
Measuring Angles.explain: First centre the protractor on the vertex, then align the base line with one arm, then read where the other arm crosses the scale.

Perpendicular Lines.q: Two lines are called perpendicular if they intersect and form an angle of:
Perpendicular Lines.explain: Perpendicular lines must intersect and form exactly a 90° (right) angle.

Perpendicular Lines.q: What symbol is used to show that line AB is perpendicular to line CD?
Perpendicular Lines.explain: The symbol ⊥ is used to denote perpendicularity, written as AB ⊥ CD.

Perpendicular Lines.q: Which of these pairs is definitely perpendicular?
Perpendicular Lines.explain: Only lines crossing at exactly 90° are called perpendicular.

Perpendicular Lines.q: What is a perpendicular bisector of a segment?
opts: Any line that touches the segment once
A line that is perpendicular AND passes through the segment’s midpoint
A line parallel to the segment
Perpendicular Lines.explain: A perpendicular bisector must satisfy two conditions: be perpendicular (90°) to the segment, and pass through its exact midpoint.

Perpendicular Lines.q: A perpendicular bisector divides a line segment into two parts that are always ____ in length.
Perpendicular Lines.explain: By definition, a bisector divides the segment into two equal halves.

Perpendicular Lines.q: If two lines cross at 75°, are they perpendicular?
opts: No, because the angle is not 90°
Yes, if they are the same length
Perpendicular Lines.explain: Crossing alone is not enough — perpendicularity requires the angle to be exactly 90°.

Perpendicular Lines.q: Which everyday example best shows perpendicular lines?
opts: The hands of a clock at 11 o’clock
A wall meeting the floor at a right angle
Perpendicular Lines.explain: A wall meeting the floor typically forms a 90° angle, making them perpendicular.

Perpendicular Lines.q: A line crosses a segment at exactly its midpoint but at an angle of 70°, not 90°. Can we call it a perpendicular bisector? (type yes or no)
Perpendicular Lines.explain: Even though it passes through the midpoint, it is NOT a perpendicular bisector unless the angle is exactly 90°.

Perpendicular Lines.q: A line crosses a segment at exactly 90° but NOT at its midpoint. What can we call this line?
opts: A perpendicular line (but not a bisector)
Perpendicular Lines.explain: It is perpendicular (since the angle is 90°) but not a bisector unless it also passes through the midpoint.

Perpendicular Lines.q: A tic-tac-toe (noughts and crosses) grid has horizontal and vertical lines crossing. What relationship do these lines typically have?
Perpendicular Lines.explain: The horizontal and vertical lines of a tic-tac-toe grid typically cross at 90°, making them perpendicular.

Perpendicular Lines.q: A carpenter checks that a table leg meets the tabletop at exactly 90° using a set-square. What word describes this leg-to-tabletop relationship?
Perpendicular Lines.explain: A leg meeting the tabletop at exactly 90° is described as being perpendicular to it.

Perpendicular Lines.q: Two lines are perpendicular. How many right angles are formed in total at their intersection point?
Perpendicular Lines.explain: When two lines cross perpendicularly, they create 4 right angles around the intersection point.

Perpendicular Lines.q: A road crosses a railway track at exactly 90°, forming a level crossing. What term describes this road-track relationship?
Perpendicular Lines.explain: A road crossing a railway track at exactly 90° is described as perpendicular to it.

Perpendicular Lines.q: How many degrees total are formed by ALL FOUR angles around the intersection point of two perpendicular lines?
Perpendicular Lines.explain: The four 90° angles around the intersection point add up to 360° (a complete turn), since 90×4=360.

Perpendicular Lines.q: A perpendicular bisector of segment AB also creates which special pair of equal lengths?
opts: Two equal angles only, not lengths
Two equal halves of segment AB (the midpoint divides it equally)
Perpendicular Lines.explain: Since it passes through the midpoint, the perpendicular bisector creates two equal halves of the original segment.

Perpendicular Lines.q: An artist draws a perfect plus-sign (+) shape. What can you say about the two strokes forming the plus sign, if they cross at exactly 90° through each other’s centre?
opts: They are perpendicular bisectors of each other
Perpendicular Lines.explain: If both strokes cross at 90° through each other’s midpoints, each is a perpendicular bisector of the other.

Perpendicular Lines.q: A flagpole stands perfectly vertical, meeting the flat horizontal ground. What single word describes the angle relationship between the flagpole and the ground?
Perpendicular Lines.explain: A vertical flagpole meeting flat horizontal ground typically forms a 90° angle, making them perpendicular.

Perpendicular Lines.q: Which statement is TRUE about perpendicular lines?
opts: They are always the same length
Perpendicular Lines.explain: By definition, perpendicular lines meet and form exactly a 90° angle.

Perpendicular Lines.q: A window frame has a vertical bar and a horizontal bar crossing it, forming four equal-looking right-angle corners. What relationship do the two bars have?
opts: They are parallel to each other
Perpendicular Lines.explain: Bars forming four right-angle corners where they cross are perpendicular to each other.

Perpendicular Lines.q: Arrange these angle-pairs from the angle CLOSEST to perpendicular (90°) to the FARTHEST: 60°, 88°, 130°.
Perpendicular Lines.explain: 88° is closest to 90°, then 60° (30° away), then 130° (40° away) is farthest.

Classification of Triangles.q: A triangle with all 3 sides equal is called:
Classification of Triangles.explain: A triangle with all three sides equal in length is called equilateral.

Classification of Triangles.q: A triangle with exactly 2 sides equal is called:
Classification of Triangles.explain: A triangle with exactly two equal sides is called isosceles.

Classification of Triangles.q: A triangle with all 3 sides of different lengths is called:
Classification of Triangles.explain: A triangle with no equal sides at all is called scalene.

Classification of Triangles.q: A triangle with all 3 angles acute (each less than 90°) is called:
Classification of Triangles.explain: A triangle where every angle is less than 90° is called acute-angled.

Classification of Triangles.q: A triangle with one angle exactly 90° is called:
Classification of Triangles.explain: A triangle with exactly one 90° angle is called right-angled.

Classification of Triangles.q: A triangle with one angle greater than 90° is called:
Classification of Triangles.explain: A triangle with one angle bigger than 90° (but less than 180°) is called obtuse-angled.

Classification of Triangles.q: The sum of all three angles in any triangle always equals how many degrees?
Classification of Triangles.explain: The three interior angles of any triangle always add up to exactly 180°.

Classification of Triangles.q: Why can a triangle never have TWO right angles?
opts: It is just a rule with no reason
Two 90° angles alone would total 180°, leaving 0° for the third angle, which is impossible
Triangles can actually have two right angles
Classification of Triangles.explain: Since all three angles must sum to 180°, two 90° angles would use up the entire 180° budget, leaving no room for a third angle.

Classification of Triangles.q: An equilateral triangle’s three angles are always:
Classification of Triangles.explain: Since all sides are equal, all angles are also equal — each measuring 180°÷3=60°.

Classification of Triangles.q: A triangle has angles of 90°, 50°, and 40°. What type of triangle is this (by angle, one word)?
Classification of Triangles.explain: Since one angle is exactly 90°, this is a right-angled triangle.

Classification of Triangles.q: A triangle has sides of length 5cm, 5cm, and 8cm. What type is it (by sides)?
Classification of Triangles.explain: Two sides (5cm and 5cm) are equal, making it isosceles.

Classification of Triangles.q: A triangle has sides of length 4cm, 6cm, and 9cm. What type is it (by sides)?
Classification of Triangles.explain: All three sides have different lengths, making it scalene.

Classification of Triangles.q: A triangle has angles of 100°, 50°, and 30°. What type is it (by angle)?
Classification of Triangles.explain: One angle (100°) is more than 90°, making it obtuse-angled.

Classification of Triangles.q: An equilateral triangle is ALWAYS also a(n) ____-angled triangle, since all its angles are 60°.
Classification of Triangles.explain: Since 60° is less than 90°, an equilateral triangle is always acute-angled too.

Classification of Triangles.q: A road warning sign is shaped like a triangle with all three sides exactly equal. What is this triangle called by its sides?
Classification of Triangles.explain: A triangle with all three sides equal is equilateral.
