Classification of Triangles.q: A slice cut diagonally from a square sandwich has two equal sides (the original square’s edges) and one longer diagonal side. What type of triangle is this (by sides)?
Classification of Triangles.explain: Two sides are equal (from the square’s edges), making this an isosceles triangle.

Classification of Triangles.q: A carpenter builds a wooden support brace with a 90° corner where two beams meet, and a third diagonal beam. What type of triangle (by angle) is formed?
Classification of Triangles.explain: Since there is a 90° angle, this is a right-angled triangle.

Classification of Triangles.q: A triangle-shaped roof has angles measuring 80°, 60°, and 40°. What type is this triangle by its angles (one word)?
Classification of Triangles.explain: All three angles (80°, 60°, 40°) are less than 90°, making this acute-angled.

Classification of Triangles.q: Can a single triangle be BOTH isosceles AND right-angled at the same time?
opts: Yes — these are two separate classification systems (by sides, by angles) that can combine
Only equilateral triangles can be right-angled
Classification of Triangles.explain: Side-classification and angle-classification are independent — a triangle can be isosceles (2 equal sides) AND right-angled (one 90° angle) simultaneously.

Classification of Triangles.q: Arrange these triangle angle-sets from MOST acute (smallest largest-angle) to MOST obtuse (largest largest-angle): {60,60,60}, {100,50,30}, {80,60,40}.
Classification of Triangles.explain: Comparing the largest angle in each set: 60° (acute) < 80° (still acute, but closer to 90°) < 100° (obtuse) — from most acute to most obtuse.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: A quadrilateral has how many sides?
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: A quadrilateral is defined as a closed figure with exactly 4 sides.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: The four interior angles of any quadrilateral always add up to how many degrees?
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: The interior angles of any quadrilateral always sum to exactly 360°.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: What is a parallelogram?
opts: A quadrilateral with no parallel sides
A quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides parallel
A quadrilateral with only one pair of parallel sides
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: A parallelogram has both pairs of opposite sides parallel and equal.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: What makes a rectangle special among parallelograms?
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: A rectangle is a parallelogram in which all four angles measure exactly 90°.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: What makes a square special among rectangles?
opts: It has all four sides equal in addition to all 90° angles
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: A square is a rectangle that ALSO has all four sides equal in length.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: What is a rhombus?
opts: A parallelogram with all four sides equal (angles may not be 90°)
A quadrilateral with no equal sides
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: A rhombus is a parallelogram with all four sides equal in length, though its angles don’t have to be 90°.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: What is a trapezium?
opts: A quadrilateral with both pairs of sides parallel
A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of opposite sides parallel
A quadrilateral with no sides parallel
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: A trapezium has exactly ONE pair of opposite sides parallel, unlike a parallelogram.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: Is every square also a rhombus? (type yes or no)
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: A square has all four sides equal, which satisfies the definition of a rhombus too.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: Is every rhombus also a square?
opts: No, only if its angles are also all 90°
No, a rhombus never has equal sides
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: A rhombus only becomes a square if its angles are also all 90° — otherwise it stays a "tilted" rhombus.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: A quadrilateral has angles of 90°, 90°, 90°, and 90°. What MUST it be?
opts: A rectangle (possibly a square if sides are also equal)
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: Four 90° angles always make it a rectangle (a special parallelogram); it’s also a square if the sides happen to be equal too.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: A quadrilateral has angles 100°, 80°, 100°, and 80°. These add up to how many degrees in total?
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: 100+80+100+80=360°, confirming the angle-sum rule for any quadrilateral.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: A phone screen is rectangular, with all four corners exactly 90°, but its length and width differ. Is this shape a square?
opts: No, since not all sides are equal
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: Since the length and width differ, not all four sides are equal, so it is a rectangle but NOT a square.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: A diamond-shaped kite has all four sides exactly equal but its angles are not all 90°. What shape is this most likely?
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: Equal sides with non-90° angles describes a rhombus.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: A table’s top has one pair of parallel edges but the other pair is NOT parallel. What is this shape called (one word)?
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: A quadrilateral with only one pair of parallel sides is called a trapezium.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: Which shape is BOTH a rhombus AND a rectangle at the same time?
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: A square satisfies both conditions: all sides equal (rhombus) and all angles 90° (rectangle).

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: A quadrilateral has 3 angles measuring 85°, 95°, and 100°. What is the 4th angle?
A road sign shaped like a quadrilateral has both pairs of opposite sides parallel and equal, but its angles are 70° and 110° (alternating). What is this shape?
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: Both pairs of sides being parallel and equal makes it a parallelogram, but since the angles aren’t 90°, it is not a rectangle.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: A garden plot is shaped like a quadrilateral with all four sides exactly 8 metres and all four angles exactly 90°. What is the precise name for this shape (one word)?
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: Equal sides AND 90° angles together define a square specifically.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: Which of the following is TRUE about all quadrilaterals, regardless of type?
opts: Their interior angles always sum to 360°
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: No matter the specific type, every quadrilateral’s four interior angles always sum to 360°.

Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.q: Arrange these shapes from MOST specific/restrictive to LEAST specific (most general): Quadrilateral, Square, Rectangle.
Quadrilaterals::Understanding Elementary.explain: Square is the most specific (most properties required), then Rectangle (fewer requirements), then Quadrilateral (the broadest, most general category).

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: What is a polygon?
opts: A closed figure made entirely of straight line segments
An open shape with no boundary
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: A polygon is a closed figure made only of straight line segments — no curves allowed.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: What is a polygon with 5 sides called?
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: A 5-sided polygon is called a pentagon.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: What is a polygon with 6 sides called?
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: A 6-sided polygon is called a hexagon.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: What is a polygon with 8 sides called?
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: An 8-sided polygon is called an octagon.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: What is a polygon with 7 sides called?
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: A 7-sided polygon is called a heptagon.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: A polygon with 6 sides always has exactly how many vertices?
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: For any polygon, the number of sides always equals the number of vertices.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: What defines a REGULAR polygon?
opts: All sides equal AND all angles equal
It must have an even number of sides
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: A regular polygon requires both equal side lengths and equal angles throughout.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: What is an irregular polygon?
opts: A polygon whose sides and/or angles are not all equal
A polygon with fewer than 3 sides
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: An irregular polygon has sides and/or angles that are not all the same.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: A triangle has exactly how many diagonals?
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: A triangle has zero diagonals because all its vertices are already directly connected by sides.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: What is a diagonal of a polygon?
opts: A line segment connecting two non-adjacent vertices
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: A diagonal connects two vertices that are NOT already joined by a side.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: A quadrilateral has how many diagonals?
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: A quadrilateral has exactly 2 diagonals, connecting each pair of opposite corners.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: A stop sign has 8 equal sides and 8 equal angles. What is this shape called?
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: 8 equal sides and angles describes a regular octagon, like a stop sign.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: A honeycomb cell has 6 sides. What is this shape called?
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: A honeycomb cell is a hexagon, having 6 sides.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: A soccer ball’s white panels typically have 5 sides each. What is this shape called (one word)?
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: A 5-sided shape is called a pentagon, matching the soccer ball’s white panels.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: Why does a triangle have no diagonals at all?
opts: Because all 3 of its vertices are already connected directly by sides
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: Since a triangle’s 3 vertices are all already joined by sides, there are no remaining non-adjacent vertex pairs to connect.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: A traffic island is shaped with 5 sides, but each side is a different length and the angles are all different too. What kind of polygon is this?
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: Different side lengths and angles make this an irregular pentagon.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: For ANY polygon, what is always true about the number of sides, vertices, and angles?
opts: They are always equal to each other
Vertices are always double the sides
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: For any polygon, the number of sides always equals the number of vertices and the number of angles.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: A floor tile is shaped like a perfect hexagon with all 6 sides and angles equal. What TYPE of polygon is this specifically (one word)?
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: Equal sides and equal angles together describe a regular polygon.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: A pentagon has how many vertices?
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: A pentagon, having 5 sides, also has exactly 5 vertices.

Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.q: Arrange these shapes from FEWEST sides to MOST sides: hexagon, pentagon, octagon, triangle.
Polygons::Understanding Elementary Shape.explain: Triangle (3) → Pentagon (5) → Hexagon (6) → Octagon (8), from fewest to most sides.

3D Shapes.q: What are the flat or curved surfaces of a 3D shape called?
3D Shapes.explain: The surfaces (flat or curved) of a solid shape are called its faces.

3D Shapes.q: What is the line segment where two faces of a solid meet called?
3D Shapes.explain: An edge is the line segment where two faces of a solid shape meet.

3D Shapes.q: What is the corner point where edges meet on a solid called?
3D Shapes.explain: A vertex is the corner point where edges of a solid shape meet.

3D Shapes.q: How many faces does a cube have?
3D Shapes.explain: A cube has 6 equal square faces.

3D Shapes.q: How many edges does a cube have?
3D Shapes.explain: A cube has 12 edges.

3D Shapes.q: How many vertices does a cube have?
3D Shapes.explain: A cube has 8 vertices (corners).

3D Shapes.q: What is the main difference between a cube and a cuboid?
opts: A cube’s faces are all equal squares; a cuboid’s rectangular faces are not all equal
3D Shapes.explain: Both have 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices, but a cube’s faces are all equal squares while a cuboid’s faces are rectangles that aren’t all the same size.

3D Shapes.q: How many curved surfaces and flat faces does a cylinder have?
3D Shapes.explain: A cylinder has 1 curved surface and 2 flat circular faces (top and bottom).

3D Shapes.q: How many vertices does a cylinder have (in the usual sense of sharp corners)?
3D Shapes.explain: A cylinder has no sharp vertices — its circular edges are curved, not pointed corners.

3D Shapes.q: How many flat faces, curved surfaces, and vertices does a cone have?
3D Shapes.explain: A cone has 1 flat circular face, 1 curved surface, and 1 vertex (the pointed tip).

3D Shapes.q: Which 3D shape has NO flat faces, NO edges, and NO vertices at all?
3D Shapes.explain: A sphere is entirely curved, with no flat faces, straight edges, or vertices.

3D Shapes.q: A pyramid’s triangular side faces all meet at a single point at the top. What is this point called?
3D Shapes.explain: The single top point where a pyramid’s triangular faces meet is called its vertex (or apex).

3D Shapes.q: A brick used in construction has 6 rectangular faces, not all of the same size. What 3D shape is this?
3D Shapes.explain: A brick with unequal rectangular faces is a cuboid.

3D Shapes.q: A can of soda has flat circular tops and a curved side. What 3D shape is this?
3D Shapes.explain: A can with flat circular ends and a curved side surface is a cylinder.

3D Shapes.q: A party hat is shaped with a circular base and a single pointed tip at the top. What 3D shape is this (one word)?
3D Shapes.explain: A shape with a flat circular base and one pointed vertex is a cone.

3D Shapes.q: A basketball has a completely curved surface with no flat parts at all. What 3D shape is this?
3D Shapes.explain: A completely curved shape with no flat faces is a sphere.

3D Shapes.q: A dice used in board games has all six faces as equal squares. What 3D shape is this?
3D Shapes.explain: A shape with 6 equal square faces is a cube.

3D Shapes.q: Why does a sphere have no edges, even though it has a surface?
opts: Because it has too many faces to count edges
Because its surface is entirely curved with no two flat faces meeting anywhere
Because spheres are not real 3D shapes
3D Shapes.explain: Edges form where two FLAT faces meet; since a sphere’s surface is entirely curved with no flat faces, it has no edges.

3D Shapes.q: The Great Pyramid of Giza has a square base and four triangular faces meeting at a single top point. What 3D shape is this?
3D Shapes.explain: A shape with a polygon base and triangular faces meeting at one top vertex is a pyramid.

3D Shapes.q: Arrange these 3D shapes from FEWEST vertices to MOST vertices: cube, sphere, cone.
3D Shapes.explain: Sphere (0 vertices) → Cone (1 vertex) → Cube (8 vertices), from fewest to most.

Representing Integers.q: What are integers?
opts: Whole numbers and their negatives, including zero
Representing Integers.explain: Integers include all whole numbers, their negative counterparts, and zero.

Representing Integers.q: Is zero a positive integer, a negative integer, or neither?
Representing Integers.explain: Zero is neither positive nor negative — it sits exactly at the boundary.

Representing Integers.q: How is a negative integer always written?
Representing Integers.explain: A negative integer must always carry a minus (−) sign — it is never optional.

Representing Integers.q: A temperature of 5°C below zero is written as which integer?
Representing Integers.explain: Below zero means negative, so it is written as −5.

Representing Integers.q: A profit of ₹300 is written as the integer ____ (include the sign if needed).
Representing Integers.explain: A profit (a gain) is represented by a positive integer, +300 (the plus sign can also be omitted since plain numbers are assumed positive).

Representing Integers.q: A loss of ₹150 in a business is written as which integer?
Representing Integers.explain: A loss represents a negative quantity, so it is written as −150.

Representing Integers.q: A lift goes 4 floors below the ground floor. What integer represents this position?
Representing Integers.explain: Going below the ground floor (the zero point) is represented by the negative integer −4.

Representing Integers.q: A lift goes 4 floors above the ground floor. What integer represents this position?
opts: It cannot be written as an integer
Representing Integers.explain: Going above the ground floor is represented by the positive integer +4.

Representing Integers.q: Mount Everest’s height is about 8,849m above sea level. As an integer (just the number, with sign), this is written as ____.
Representing Integers.explain: Above sea level means a positive integer, +8849 (sign can be omitted since positive is the default).

Representing Integers.q: Why does a negative integer always need its minus sign written, while a positive integer’s plus sign is often left out?
opts: Because leaving out the minus sign would completely change the number’s meaning and direction
Because positive numbers don’t actually have a sign at all
Representing Integers.explain: Omitting the minus sign would make a negative number look positive, completely changing its meaning, so it must always be written.

Representing Integers.q: A submarine descends to 200m below sea level. Which integer represents its position?
Representing Integers.explain: Below sea level is represented by the negative integer −200.

Representing Integers.q: A hot air balloon rises to 500m above the ground. Which integer represents its height?
Representing Integers.explain: Above the ground (the zero point) is represented by the positive integer +500.

Representing Integers.q: A football team gains 12 yards on a play. As an integer (with sign), this gain is written as ____.
Representing Integers.explain: A gain in yards is represented by a positive integer, +12.

Representing Integers.q: A football team loses 8 yards on a play. As an integer, this is written as:
Representing Integers.explain: A loss in yards is represented by the negative integer −8.

Representing Integers.q: Which of these is NOT a valid way to think about integers?
opts: Whole numbers extended to include negatives
Numbers that always have a fractional part
Numbers used to represent opposite directions from zero
Representing Integers.explain: Integers are whole numbers (and their negatives) — they never include fractional or decimal parts.

Representing Integers.q: A bank account is overdrawn by ₹500 (the owner owes the bank). What integer represents this balance?
Representing Integers.explain: Owing money (being overdrawn) is represented by the negative integer −500.

Representing Integers.q: A scuba diver is swimming 18m below the surface of the water. As an integer (with sign), this depth is written as ____.
Representing Integers.explain: Below the surface (the zero point) is represented by the negative integer −18.

Representing Integers.q: A thermometer reads exactly 0°C. What can we say about this temperature as an integer?
opts: It is neither positive nor negative
Representing Integers.explain: Zero is neither positive nor negative, even though it is a valid integer.

Representing Integers.q: The Dead Sea shore is about 430m below sea level, one of the lowest points on Earth’s land surface. What integer represents this elevation?
Representing Integers.explain: Below sea level is represented by the negative integer −430.

Representing Integers.q: Arrange these real-life situations from MOST NEGATIVE to MOST POSITIVE integer value: a mountain peak at +2000m, a basement at −15m, sea level at 0m.
Representing Integers.explain: −15 (basement) < 0 (sea level) < +2000 (mountain peak), from most negative to most positive.

Integers on the Number Line.q: On a number line, where do positive integers go?
Integers on the Number Line.explain: Positive integers are placed to the right of zero on a number line.

Integers on the Number Line.q: On a number line, where do negative integers go?
Integers on the Number Line.explain: Negative integers are placed to the left of zero on a number line.

Integers on the Number Line.q: To plot the integer −4, you start at 0 and:
Integers on the Number Line.explain: To plot a negative integer, count that many equal steps to the LEFT of zero.

Integers on the Number Line.q: What is the distance of −6 from zero (ignoring sign)?
Integers on the Number Line.explain: Distance ignores the sign, so −6 is 6 steps away from zero.

Integers on the Number Line.q: What is the opposite of the integer 7?
Integers on the Number Line.explain: The opposite of 7 is −7 — same distance from zero, opposite direction.

Integers on the Number Line.q: What is the opposite of the integer −9?
Integers on the Number Line.explain: The opposite of −9 is 9 (or +9).

Integers on the Number Line.q: Which integer is its own opposite?
Integers on the Number Line.explain: Zero is the only integer that is its own opposite, since it has no direction or distance to flip.

Integers on the Number Line.q: On a number line, which integer is greater: −2 or −9?
Integers on the Number Line.explain: −2 is further right than −9, so −2 is the greater integer.

Integers on the Number Line.q: On a number line, which integer is greater: 3 or −10?
Integers on the Number Line.explain: Every positive integer is greater than every negative integer, so 3 > −10.

Integers on the Number Line.q: Between −15 and −3, which integer is greater (write just the number)?
Integers on the Number Line.explain: −3 is closer to zero (further right) than −15, making −3 the greater integer.

Integers on the Number Line.q: What is true about the distances of opposite integers (like +6 and −6) from zero?
Integers on the Number Line.explain: Opposite integers are always the same distance from zero, just in opposite directions.

Integers on the Number Line.q: A diver is at −12m and a bird is at +12m (relative to sea level at 0). What is true about their distances from sea level?
opts: The diver is farther from sea level
The bird is farther from sea level
They are exactly the same distance from sea level
Integers on the Number Line.explain: Both −12 and +12 are exactly 12 units from zero — the same distance, just opposite directions.

Integers on the Number Line.q: Which integer lies exactly halfway between −4 and 0 on a number line?
Integers on the Number Line.explain: Halfway between −4 and 0 is −2 (since −2 is 2 steps from each).

Integers on the Number Line.q: Which integer lies exactly halfway between 0 and 8 on a number line?
Integers on the Number Line.explain: Halfway between 0 and 8 is 4.

Integers on the Number Line.q: On a thermometer-style number line, which is colder: −15°C or −8°C?
Integers on the Number Line.explain: −15 is further left (smaller) than −8, so −15°C is colder.

Integers on the Number Line.q: What general rule lets you instantly compare any two integers using a number line?
opts: The integer further right is always smaller
The integer further right is always greater
You cannot compare integers using a number line
Integers on the Number Line.explain: No matter the signs involved, the integer positioned further to the right on a number line is always the greater one.

Integers on the Number Line.q: A hiker is at an elevation of −50m (below a reference point) and another hiker is at +20m. Who is at the higher position?
opts: They are at the same height
Integers on the Number Line.explain: +20 is greater than −50 (positive is always greater than negative), so that hiker is higher up.

Integers on the Number Line.q: A weather station records −3°C and −11°C on two different days. Which reading represents the WARMER day (write just the number)?
Integers on the Number Line.explain: −3 is greater (further right, closer to zero) than −11, so −3°C is the warmer temperature.

Integers on the Number Line.q: On a number line, is −1 closer to zero or farther from zero compared to −100?
Integers on the Number Line.explain: −1 is only 1 step from zero, while −100 is 100 steps from zero — so −1 is much closer to zero.

Integers on the Number Line.q: Arrange these number-line positions from LEFTMOST to RIGHTMOST: −2, 5, −9, 0.
Integers on the Number Line.explain: −9 → −2 → 0 → 5, from leftmost (smallest) to rightmost (largest) on the number line.

Addition of Integers.q: When adding a POSITIVE integer on a number line, which direction do you hop?
Addition of Integers.explain: Adding a positive integer means hopping to the RIGHT that many steps.

Addition of Integers.q: When adding a NEGATIVE integer on a number line, which direction do you hop?
Addition of Integers.explain: Adding a negative integer means hopping to the LEFT that many steps.

Addition of Integers.q: What is 5 + 3?
Addition of Integers.explain: Both positive, so simply add: 5+3=8.
Both negative: add the values (5+3=8) and keep the negative sign: −8.
Add 10 and 7 to get 17, keep the negative sign: −17.

Addition of Integers.q: What is 8 + (−3)?
Addition of Integers.explain: Different signs: 8 is bigger, so subtract 8−3=5, keep positive sign: 5.

Addition of Integers.q: What is (−8) + 3?
Addition of Integers.explain: Different signs: 8 is bigger (and negative), so subtract 8−3=5, keep negative sign: −5.

Addition of Integers.q: What is 15 + (−9)?
Addition of Integers.explain: Different signs: 15 is bigger, subtract 15−9=6, keep positive sign: 6.

Addition of Integers.q: What is (−15) + 9?
Addition of Integers.explain: Different signs: 15 is bigger (and negative), subtract 15−9=6, keep negative sign: −6.

Addition of Integers.q: What is the rule for adding two integers with the SAME sign?
opts: Add their values and keep the common sign
Addition of Integers.explain: When signs match, add the values together and keep that same sign for the answer.

Addition of Integers.q: What is the rule for adding two integers with DIFFERENT signs?
opts: Subtract the smaller value from the bigger value and keep the sign of the bigger value
Addition of Integers.explain: Subtract the smaller value (ignoring signs) from the bigger value, and use the sign of whichever was originally bigger.

Addition of Integers.q: A temperature starts at 4°C and drops by 9 degrees. What is the new temperature, written as an addition of integers?
Addition of Integers.explain: A drop of 9 degrees is adding −9: 4 + (−9) = −5°C.

Addition of Integers.q: A football team loses 5 yards, then gains 12 yards on the next play. What is their total yard change?
Addition of Integers.explain: (−5) + 12: 12 is bigger, subtract 12−5=7, keep positive sign: +7 yards gained.

Addition of Integers.q: A submarine at −80m dives another 25m deeper. What is its new depth (as an integer)?
Addition of Integers.explain: Diving deeper adds another negative: (−80) + (−25) = −105m.

Addition of Integers.q: What is 0 + (−7)?
Addition of Integers.explain: Adding zero to any integer doesn’t change it: 0 + (−7) = −7.

Addition of Integers.q: What is (−6) + 6?
Addition of Integers.explain: Adding opposite integers always gives zero: (−6) + 6 = 0.

Addition of Integers.q: A hiker climbs 200m, then descends 350m. What is their overall change in elevation?
Addition of Integers.explain: 200 + (−350): 350 is bigger, subtract 350−200=150, keep negative sign (since 350 was negative): −150m.

Addition of Integers.q: A bank account starts at −₹200 (overdrawn) and a deposit of ₹500 is made. What is the new balance (as an integer)?
Addition of Integers.explain: (−200) + 500: 500 is bigger, subtract 500−200=300, keep positive sign: +300.

Addition of Integers.q: Why does adding an integer and its opposite always give zero?
opts: Because opposite integers always cancel out, being equal distances in opposite directions
Because zero is a special exception with no rule
Addition of Integers.explain: Opposite integers are equal distances from zero in opposite directions, so adding them perfectly cancels out to zero.

Addition of Integers.q: What is the additive inverse of 14?
Addition of Integers.explain: The additive inverse of 14 is −14, since 14 + (−14) = 0.

Addition of Integers.q: What is the additive inverse of −30?
Addition of Integers.explain: Flip the sign: the additive inverse of −30 is 30, since (−30) + 30 = 0.

Addition of Integers.q: What is the additive inverse of 0?
opts: There is no additive inverse of 0
Addition of Integers.explain: The additive inverse of 0 is 0 itself, since 0 + 0 = 0.

Addition of Integers.q: A series of temperature changes occur in order: starts at 0°C, then +5, then −12, then +3. Arrange the RUNNING TOTALS after each step from LOWEST to HIGHEST: after step 1 (+5), after step 2 (+5−12), after step 3 (+5−12+3).
Addition of Integers.explain: After step 1: 0+5=5. After step 2: 5+(−12)=−7. After step 3: −7+3=−4. Lowest to highest: −7, −4, 5.

Subtraction of Integers.q: What is the rule for subtracting integers?
Subtraction of Integers.explain: Subtracting an integer is the same as adding its opposite: a − b = a + (−b).
5 − (−3) = 5 + 3 = 8. Subtracting a negative becomes adding a positive.

Subtraction of Integers.q: Subtracting a negative integer is the same as:
Subtraction of Integers.explain: Subtracting a negative flips to adding a positive — two negatives combine into a positive operation.

Subtraction of Integers.q: What are the 3 steps to subtract integers?
opts: Keep the first number, change − to +, change the second number to its opposite
Subtraction of Integers.explain: The 3-step method: keep the first integer, change subtraction to addition, and flip the second integer to its opposite.

Subtraction of Integers.q: The temperature was 3°C, and it drops by 7 degrees more than that drop again (i.e., it falls further to reach a temperature that is 7 less than 3). Written as subtraction, what is 3 − 7?
A submarine at −20m needs to find how much shallower a point at −5m is. What subtraction finds this difference? (−5) − (−20) = ?
Subtraction of Integers.explain: (−5) − (−20) = (−5) + 20 = 15, meaning −5m is 15m shallower (closer to the surface) than −20m.

Subtraction of Integers.q: A bank balance is ₹50. After a fee, the new balance is found by subtracting: 50 − 80. What is the result?
A hiker at +800m wants to know how much higher they are than a hiker at −200m. What subtraction finds this? 800 − (−200) = ?

Subtraction of Integers.explain: (−15) − (−15) = (−15) + 15 = 0. Subtracting an integer from itself always gives zero.

Subtraction of Integers.q: Why does subtracting an integer from itself always equal zero?
opts: Because zero is always the answer to subtraction
Because the integer and its opposite cancel out when you apply the subtraction rule
It does not always equal zero
Subtraction of Integers.explain: a − a = a + (−a), and an integer plus its own opposite always equals zero.

Subtraction of Integers.q: Arrange these subtraction results from SMALLEST to LARGEST: 5 − 9, 5 − (−9), 5 − 0.

Ordering Integers.q: What does the symbol > mean?
Ordering Integers.explain: > means "greater than".

Ordering Integers.q: What does the symbol < mean?
Ordering Integers.explain: < means "less than".

Ordering Integers.q: Which is true: 5 ___ 2?
Ordering Integers.explain: 5 is to the right of 2 on a number line, so 5 > 2.

Ordering Integers.q: Which is true: −8 ___ −1?
Ordering Integers.explain: −8 is to the left of −1 on a number line, so −8 < −1.

Ordering Integers.q: Fill in the correct symbol (> or <): −3 ___ 4
Ordering Integers.explain: −3 is to the left of 4, so −3 < 4.

Ordering Integers.q: Which of these is TRUE for any positive and any negative integer?
opts: The positive integer is always greater
The negative integer is always greater
It depends on the specific numbers
Ordering Integers.explain: Every positive integer is always greater than every negative integer, no matter their specific values.

Ordering Integers.q: Among −2, −9, and −5, which is the SMALLEST?
Ordering Integers.explain: −9 is furthest left (most negative), making it the smallest.

Ordering Integers.q: Among −2, −9, and −5, which is the LARGEST?
Ordering Integers.explain: −2 is furthest right (closest to zero among these), making it the largest.

Ordering Integers.q: Order these from smallest to largest: 3, −7, 0. (Write just the smallest one)
Ordering Integers.explain: The smallest of 3, −7, 0 is −7, since it is furthest left on the number line.

Ordering Integers.q: What is "ascending order"?
Ordering Integers.explain: Ascending order arranges numbers from smallest to largest.

Ordering Integers.q: What is "descending order"?
Ordering Integers.explain: Descending order arranges numbers from largest to smallest.

Ordering Integers.q: Arrange −4, 6, −1, 0 in ascending order:
Ordering Integers.explain: Ascending (smallest to largest): −4, −1, 0, 6.

Ordering Integers.q: Arrange −4, 6, −1, 0 in descending order:
Ordering Integers.explain: Descending (largest to smallest): 6, 0, −1, −4.

Ordering Integers.q: Two temperatures are recorded: −12°C and −5°C. Which represents the WARMER temperature?
Ordering Integers.explain: −5 is greater than −12 (closer to zero), so −5°C is warmer.

Ordering Integers.q: A submarine is at −60m and another is at −90m. Which submarine is CLOSER to the surface (write just the number)?
Ordering Integers.explain: −60 is greater than −90 (closer to zero/the surface), so the submarine at −60m is closer to the surface.

Ordering Integers.q: Why is "the digit being bigger" NOT the same as "the integer being bigger" when comparing negative numbers?
opts: They are actually always the same thing
For negative integers, a BIGGER digit means a SMALLER (more negative) value
Negative integers cannot be compared at all
Ordering Integers.explain: For negative integers, a bigger digit (ignoring sign) actually represents a position further left, making it a SMALLER value, not a bigger one.

Ordering Integers.q: Three students’ bank balances are: −₹200, +₹50, −₹500. Who has the MOST money (highest balance)?
Ordering Integers.explain: +50 is greater than both negative balances, since any positive integer beats any negative integer.

Ordering Integers.q: Which list is correctly arranged in DESCENDING order?
Ordering Integers.explain: Descending order goes from largest to smallest: 10, 5, 0, −5, −10.

Ordering Integers.q: Four hikers are at elevations +500m, −100m, +1200m, −50m. What is the elevation of the HIGHEST hiker (write just the number)?
Ordering Integers.explain: +1200 is the greatest of the four values, since it is the most positive (furthest right on a number line).

Ordering Integers.q: Arrange these account balances in ASCENDING order (smallest/most negative first): +200, −450, +50, −100.
Ordering Integers.explain: Ascending order: −450, −100, +50, +200, from smallest to largest.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: A lift starts at the 3rd floor (+3), goes down 7 floors, then up 2 floors. Where does it end up?
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.explain: 3 + (−7) = −4, then (−4) + 2 = −2. The lift ends at the 2nd basement floor.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: Town A is at +850m elevation and Town B is at −200m elevation. What is the DIFFERENCE in their elevations (Town A minus Town B)?
A diver at −18m rises 5m, then dives down another 11m. What integer represents her final depth?
A question asks “how much colder is −15°C than 3°C?” Which calculation answers it?
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.explain: “How much colder” means the difference, found by subtracting: (−15) − 3 = −18, meaning 18 degrees colder.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: A game starts a player at 0 points. They gain 25, lose 40, then gain 10. What is their final score?
Which integer is the additive inverse of the final answer to: 8 + (−8)?
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.explain: 8 + (−8) = 0, and the additive inverse of 0 is 0 itself.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: A submarine at −40m and another at −65m: which is CLOSER to the surface, and by how many metres?
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.explain: −40 is greater (closer to 0/the surface) than −65. Difference: (−40) − (−65) = 25m.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: A hot air balloon at 0m rises 300m, descends 450m, then rises 80m. What is its final height?
To order −6, 4, −1, 0 from largest to smallest, what is the FIRST (largest) number?
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.explain: 4 is the only positive integer in the list, making it the largest.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: A company’s profit/loss over 3 months: +₹4000, −₹9000, +₹2000. What is the OVERALL result?
What is the additive inverse of the integer that represents “20m below sea level”?
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.explain: “20m below sea level” is −20. Its additive inverse is +20 (flip the sign).

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: A hiker’s elevation changes over 4 stages: +600m, −250m, +400m, −900m. Is the hiker higher or lower than the start, and by how much?
Which calculation correctly finds how much MORE +12 is than −9?
A bank account at −₹300 receives a deposit of ₹450, then a withdrawal of ₹600. What is the final balance?
Among the depths −120m, −45m, and −80m, which represents the SHALLOWEST point?
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.explain: −45 is the greatest (closest to zero) of the three, so it is the shallowest.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: A weather station records temperature changes of −3°, +7°, −5°, +2° across 4 readings, starting from 10°C. What is the FINAL temperature?
A number line problem: start at −5, add the additive inverse of −5, then subtract 3. What is the final answer?
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.explain: The additive inverse of −5 is +5. So: (−5) + 5 = 0, then 0 − 3 = −3.

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: A spacecraft’s altitude (relative to a reference point) changes as: +2000m, −3500m, +1800m. Final altitude relative to the reference point?
A diver’s depths at 3 checkpoints are calculated as: 0+(−20)=−20, (−20)+8=−12, (−12)+(−15)=−27. Arrange these three checkpoint depths from SHALLOWEST to DEEPEST.
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.explain: Shallowest to deepest means largest to smallest integer: −12 (checkpoint 2), then −20 (checkpoint 1), then −27 (checkpoint 3).

Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.q: Why must you always identify the “zero point” (like sea level or ground floor) FIRST when solving an integer word problem?
opts: Because every other value in the problem is measured relative to that zero point
Because the zero point changes the rules of addition
It isn’t actually necessary to identify it
Mixed Practice: Integers in Action.explain: All integers in a real-world problem describe positions or changes RELATIVE to an agreed zero point, so identifying it correctly is the foundation for every other step.

Types of Fractions.q: What does a fraction represent?
Types of Fractions.explain: A fraction represents a part of a whole, formed when something is divided into equal parts.

Types of Fractions.q: In the fraction 3/5, what is the number 5 called?
Types of Fractions.explain: 5 is the denominator — it tells the total number of equal parts.

Types of Fractions.q: In the fraction 3/5, what is the number 3 called?
Types of Fractions.explain: 3 is the numerator — it tells how many of the equal parts we are considering.

Types of Fractions.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. If you eat 3 slices, what fraction of the pizza did you eat?
Types of Fractions.explain: You ate 3 out of the 8 equal slices, so the fraction is 3/8.

Types of Fractions.q: What does the denominator of a fraction tell us?
opts: The total number of equal parts the whole is divided into
Types of Fractions.explain: The denominator shows the total number of equal parts the whole has been divided into.

Types of Fractions.q: What does the numerator of a fraction tell us?
opts: How many of the equal parts are being considered
Types of Fractions.explain: The numerator shows how many of the total equal parts we are talking about.

Types of Fractions.q: A chocolate bar has 6 equal pieces. If 2 pieces are eaten, what fraction of the bar is eaten?
Types of Fractions.explain: 2 out of 6 equal pieces were eaten, so the fraction is 2/6.

Types of Fractions.q: Can a fraction represent part of a GROUP of objects, not just one single shape?
opts: Yes, fractions can describe parts of a collection too
Only if the objects are identical
Types of Fractions.explain: Fractions can describe part of any whole, including a collection of objects like a group of marbles or fruits.

Types of Fractions.q: A basket has 12 oranges. If 5 are ripe, what fraction of the oranges are ripe?
Types of Fractions.explain: 5 out of the 12 total oranges are ripe, giving the fraction 5/12.

Types of Fractions.q: Which of these correctly identifies the parts of the fraction 7/9?
Types of Fractions.explain: In 7/9, the top number 7 is the numerator and the bottom number 9 is the denominator.

Types of Fractions.q: Why must the parts of a whole be EQUAL when forming a fraction?
opts: Equal parts are easier to draw
A fraction only makes sense if each part represents the same-sized share of the whole
It does not matter if parts are equal
Types of Fractions.explain: A fraction assumes each part is the same size, so the numerator correctly counts identical shares of the whole.

Types of Fractions.q: Arrange these fractions by listing their numerator and then denominator in order: the fraction 4/9.
Types of Fractions.explain: The numerator 4 comes first (top), and the denominator 9 comes second (bottom).

Types of Fractions.q: A class has 25 students. If 10 students wear glasses, what fraction of the class wears glasses?
Types of Fractions.explain: 10 students out of 25 total wear glasses, giving the fraction 10/25.

Types of Fractions.q: A cake is cut into 10 equal pieces. Riya eats 4 pieces. What fraction of the cake did Riya eat?
Types of Fractions.explain: Riya ate 4 out of the 10 equal pieces, so the fraction is 4/10.

Types of Fractions.q: A garden has 20 flowers, and 7 of them are roses. What fraction of the flowers are NOT roses?
Types of Fractions.explain: If 7 are roses, then 20−7=13 are not roses, giving the fraction 13/20.

Types of Fractions.q: A ribbon is cut into 9 equal parts. If 6 parts are used for a gift, what fraction of the ribbon is used?
Types of Fractions.explain: 6 out of the 9 equal parts are used, giving the fraction 6/9.

Types of Fractions.q: A box of 15 crayons has 9 broken ones. What fraction of the crayons are NOT broken?
Types of Fractions.explain: If 9 are broken, then 15−9=6 are not broken, giving the fraction 6/15.

Types of Fractions.q: Why is 1 sometimes written as a fraction, such as 4/4 or 7/7?
opts: It cannot be written as a fraction
When the numerator equals the denominator, all parts of the whole are included, making a complete whole (1)
Types of Fractions.explain: When numerator equals denominator, every equal part of the whole is counted, which makes exactly 1 whole.

Types of Fractions.q: A pack has 8 pencils, all of which are sharpened. What fraction of the pencils are sharpened?
Types of Fractions.explain: All 8 out of 8 pencils are sharpened, giving the fraction 8/8 (which equals 1 whole).

Types of Fractions.q: A teacher draws 3 circles on the board cut into 3, 5, and 8 equal parts respectively. Arrange the circles in order of FEWEST to MOST equal parts.
Types of Fractions.explain: 3 parts is fewest, then 5 parts, then 8 parts is the most — ordering from fewest to most.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: A proper fraction is one where:
opts: The numerator is greater than the denominator
The numerator is smaller than the denominator
Proper & Improper Fractions.explain: In a proper fraction, the numerator is smaller than the denominator, making the value less than 1.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: An improper fraction is one where:
opts: The numerator is smaller than the denominator
The numerator is greater than or equal to the denominator
Proper & Improper Fractions.explain: In an improper fraction, the numerator is greater than or equal to the denominator, making the value 1 or more.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: Which of these is a proper fraction?
Proper & Improper Fractions.explain: 5/9 has a numerator (5) smaller than its denominator (9), so it is proper.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: Which of these is an improper fraction?
Proper & Improper Fractions.explain: 9/5 has a numerator (9) greater than its denominator (5), so it is improper.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: A mixed fraction is made up of:
opts: A whole number and a proper fraction
Proper & Improper Fractions.explain: A mixed fraction combines a whole number with a proper fraction, like 2 1/3.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: Convert the improper fraction 7/3 to a mixed fraction. What is the whole number part?
Proper & Improper Fractions.explain: 7÷3=2 remainder 1, so the whole number part of the mixed fraction is 2 (giving 2 1/3).

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: Convert the improper fraction 11/4 to a mixed fraction. What is the fraction part (remainder over divisor)?
Proper & Improper Fractions.explain: 11÷4=2 remainder 3, so the fraction part is 3/4 (giving 2 3/4).

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: How do you convert a mixed fraction back to an improper fraction?
opts: Add the whole number and numerator, keep the denominator
Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, keep the denominator
Proper & Improper Fractions.explain: Multiply whole number × denominator, then add the numerator, keeping the same denominator.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: Convert the mixed fraction 3 1/2 into an improper fraction.
Convert the mixed fraction 4 2/5 into an improper fraction.
Is 8/8 a proper or improper fraction?
Proper & Improper Fractions.explain: When numerator equals denominator, the fraction equals exactly 1, which is classified as improper (numerator ≥ denominator).

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: Every improper fraction represents a value that is:
opts: Always equal to or greater than 1
Proper & Improper Fractions.explain: Improper fractions always represent values equal to or greater than 1 whole.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: Arrange these fractions from PROPER to IMPROPER: 5/3, 2/7, 6/6.
Proper & Improper Fractions.explain: 2/7 is proper (less than 1), while 5/3 and 6/6 are both improper (1 or more) — listing proper first.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: Riya ate 5 quarters of two pizzas (5/4 pizzas). Is this a proper or improper fraction, and why?
opts: Proper, because it is less than 2
Improper, because the numerator (5) is greater than the denominator (4)
Proper & Improper Fractions.explain: 5/4 has numerator greater than denominator, making it an improper fraction representing more than 1 whole pizza.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: A recipe needs 9/2 cups of flour. Express this as a mixed fraction.
Proper & Improper Fractions.explain: 9÷2=4 remainder 1, so 9/2 = 4 1/2 cups.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: A carpenter has 13/4 metres of wood. How would you express this length as a mixed number?
Proper & Improper Fractions.explain: 13÷4=3 remainder 1, so 13/4 = 3 1/4 metres.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: A jug holds 2 3/4 litres of juice. Express this as an improper fraction.
If a fraction equals exactly 3 (a whole number with no remainder), which form would correctly represent it as an improper fraction with denominator 4?
Proper & Improper Fractions.explain: 3 wholes with denominator 4 means 3×4=12, so the improper fraction is 12/4.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: A tailor uses 17/5 metres of cloth for a project. Express this as a mixed fraction.
Proper & Improper Fractions.explain: 17÷5=3 remainder 2, so 17/5 = 3 2/5 metres.

Proper & Improper Fractions.q: Three containers hold 5/2 litres, 1/2 litre, and 8/2 litres. Arrange from SMALLEST to LARGEST.
Proper & Improper Fractions.explain: 1/2 is smallest, then 5/2, then 8/2 is largest — comparing numerators since denominators are the same.

Fractions on Number Line.q: To mark the fraction 2/5 on a number line, how many equal parts should the segment from 0 to 1 be divided into?
Fractions on Number Line.explain: The denominator (5) tells us how many equal parts to divide the segment from 0 to 1 into.

Fractions on Number Line.q: To mark 3/5 on the number line (after dividing 0 to 1 into 5 equal parts), which mark do you go to?
Fractions on Number Line.explain: The numerator (3) tells us to go to the 3rd mark counting from 0.

Fractions on Number Line.q: To mark 5/6 on a number line, into how many equal parts should the gap from 0 to 1 be split?
Fractions on Number Line.explain: The denominator 6 tells us to split the gap from 0 to 1 into 6 equal parts.

Fractions on Number Line.q: On a number line, where does the fraction 1/2 lie?
Fractions on Number Line.explain: 1/2 lies exactly in the middle of the segment from 0 to 1.

Fractions on Number Line.q: Where does an improper fraction like 9/4 lie on a number line?
opts: Beyond 1, between two later whole numbers
It cannot be placed on a number line
Fractions on Number Line.explain: Since 9/4 = 2 1/4, it lies beyond 1, between the whole numbers 2 and 3.

Fractions on Number Line.q: Convert 9/4 to a mixed fraction to find which whole numbers it lies between. What is the whole number part?
Fractions on Number Line.explain: 9÷4=2 remainder 1, so 9/4 = 2 1/4, meaning the whole number part is 2.

Fractions on Number Line.q: Between which two whole numbers does 11/3 lie on the number line?
Fractions on Number Line.explain: 11÷3=3 remainder 2, so 11/3 = 3 2/3, meaning it lies between the whole numbers 3 and 4.

Fractions on Number Line.q: On a number line, if fraction A is to the RIGHT of fraction B, what can you conclude?
Fractions on Number Line.explain: A position further to the right on a number line always represents a greater value.

Fractions on Number Line.q: On a number line, 2/7 is to the left of 5/7. Which fraction is smaller?
Fractions on Number Line.explain: A fraction further to the LEFT on a number line is the smaller value, so 2/7 is smaller.

Fractions on Number Line.q: Why is the number line a useful tool for comparing fractions?
opts: It shows fractions in order of size visually, from left (smaller) to right (larger)
It only works for whole numbers
It changes the value of fractions
Fractions on Number Line.explain: The number line visually orders all numbers, including fractions, from smallest (left) to largest (right).

Fractions on Number Line.q: To mark 7/8 on a number line, you divide the segment from 0 to 1 into how many parts, and mark which one?
Fractions on Number Line.explain: Divide into 8 equal parts (denominator), then mark the 7th point from 0 (numerator).

Fractions on Number Line.q: Arrange these number-line positions for fractions from LEFT (smallest) to RIGHT (largest): 3/4, 1/4, 1/2.
Fractions on Number Line.explain: On the number line: 1/4 is leftmost, then 1/2, then 3/4 is rightmost — matching smallest to largest.

Fractions on Number Line.q: A runner has covered 5/8 of a race track. On a number line from 0 (start) to 1 (finish), where would this position be marked?
opts: Closer to the finish (1), past the halfway point
Fractions on Number Line.explain: Since 5/8 is greater than 1/2 (4/8), the position would be past the halfway mark, closer to the finish.

Fractions on Number Line.q: A glass is filled to 3/4 of its height. If the glass’s height is represented from 0 (empty) to 1 (full) on a line, how many equal parts should the line be divided into to mark this?
Fractions on Number Line.explain: The denominator 4 tells us to divide the line into 4 equal parts.

Fractions on Number Line.q: Two hikers are marked on a trail number line: Hiker A at 2/5 and Hiker B at 4/5 of the trail. Who has hiked further?
opts: They have hiked the same distance
Fractions on Number Line.explain: 4/5 is further to the right than 2/5 on the number line, so Hiker B has hiked further.

Fractions on Number Line.q: A number line marks 0, 1, and 2. If a fraction’s mark falls exactly on the tick for 1, what does that tell you about the fraction?
Fractions on Number Line.explain: If the mark falls exactly on 1, the fraction is equivalent to exactly 1 whole (like 4/4 or 5/5).

Fractions on Number Line.q: Between which two whole numbers does the improper fraction 13/5 lie?
Fractions on Number Line.explain: 13÷5=2 remainder 3, so 13/5 = 2 3/5, lying between the whole numbers 2 and 3.

Fractions on Number Line.q: A ruler marked from 0 to 1 represents a single chocolate bar. If a mark is placed at 5/6, what does this represent?
Fractions on Number Line.explain: A mark at 5/6 on a 0-to-1 line represents exactly 5/6 of the whole (the chocolate bar).

Fractions on Number Line.q: If two fractions are marked at the EXACT SAME point on a number line, what must be true about them?
opts: They must have the same denominator
Fractions on Number Line.explain: Fractions marking the exact same point on a number line represent the same value, meaning they are equivalent fractions.

Fractions on Number Line.q: Three saplings have grown to heights represented as 1/3, 5/6, and 1/2 of their maximum height. Arrange from SHORTEST to TALLEST (using their number-line positions).
Fractions on Number Line.explain: On a number line (LCM 6): 1/3=2/6, 1/2=3/6, 5/6=5/6, so shortest to tallest is 1/3, 1/2, 5/6.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.q: What are equivalent fractions?
opts: Different fractions that represent the same value
Fractions with the same numerator only
Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.explain: Equivalent fractions are fractions that may look different but represent exactly the same value.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.q: How can you create an equivalent fraction from a given fraction?
opts: Add the same number to top and bottom
Multiply (or divide) both numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number
Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.explain: Multiplying or dividing both numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number keeps the value unchanged.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.q: Find an equivalent fraction of 1/2 by multiplying numerator and denominator by 4.
Find an equivalent fraction of 3/5 by multiplying numerator and denominator by 2.
Which fraction is equivalent to 2/3?
Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.explain: 4/6 is equivalent to 2/3 because both numerator and denominator of 2/3 were multiplied by 2.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.q: A fraction is in its simplest form when:
opts: The numerator and denominator have no common factor other than 1
Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.explain: A fraction is simplest when its numerator and denominator share no common factor besides 1.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.q: Simplify the fraction 10/15 to its lowest form.
Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.explain: HCF of 10 and 15 is 5. Dividing both by 5: 10÷5=2, 15÷5=3, giving 2/3.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.q: Simplify the fraction 18/24 to its lowest form.
Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.explain: HCF of 18 and 24 is 6. Dividing both by 6: 18÷6=3, 24÷6=4, giving 3/4.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.q: To simplify a fraction, you divide the numerator and denominator by their:
Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.explain: Dividing by the Highest Common Factor (HCF) gives the simplest form of a fraction.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.q: Which of these fraction pairs are equivalent?
Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.explain: 3/4 and 9/12 are equivalent because multiplying 3/4 by 3/3 gives 9/12.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.q: Is 4/6 in its simplest form? If not, simplify it.
Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.explain: 4/6 is not simplest since HCF of 4 and 6 is 2. Dividing both by 2 gives 2/3.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.q: Arrange the steps to find an equivalent fraction of 5/7 using multiplication by 3.
Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.explain: First multiply the numerator, then the denominator, and combine to get the result 15/21.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.q: Two friends share pizzas differently: one cuts theirs into 4 slices and eats 2, the other cuts theirs into 8 slices and eats 4. Did they eat the same amount?
opts: No, the second friend ate more
Yes, 2/4 and 4/8 are equivalent fractions, both equal to half
No, the first friend ate more
Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.explain: 2/4 simplifies to 1/2, and 4/8 also simplifies to 1/2 — so both friends ate the same amount.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.q: A recipe calls for 6/8 cup of sugar. Simplify this to its lowest form.
Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.explain: HCF of 6 and 8 is 2. Dividing both by 2 gives 3/4 cup.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.q: A trader says a rope is 12/16 metres used out of the full rope. Which simpler equivalent fraction means the same amount?
Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.explain: 12/16 simplifies (divide by 4) to 3/4 — the simplest equivalent fraction.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.q: A survey shows 14/21 of students prefer cricket. Simplify this fraction.
Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.explain: HCF of 14 and 21 is 7. Dividing both by 7 gives 2/3.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.q: Why does multiplying both numerator and denominator by the same number NOT change the value of a fraction?
opts: It always makes the fraction bigger
You are essentially multiplying the fraction by 1 (since the number over itself equals 1)
Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.explain: Multiplying numerator and denominator by the same number is the same as multiplying by a form of 1 (like 3/3), so the value stays unchanged.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.q: A test result reads 20/25 marks. Simplify this fraction to its lowest form.
Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.explain: HCF of 20 and 25 is 5. Dividing both by 5 gives 4/5.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.q: A baker has two equivalent recipes calling for 1/3 and 4/12 cup of butter. Are these amounts the same?
Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.explain: 1/3 multiplied by 4/4 gives 4/12, so these are equivalent fractions representing the same amount.

Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.q: Arrange the steps to simplify 16/20 to its lowest form.
Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form.explain: First find the HCF, then divide both numbers by it, then state the simplified result.

Comparing Fractions.q: What are like fractions?
Comparing Fractions.explain: Like fractions have the same denominator, which makes them easy to compare directly.

Comparing Fractions.q: To compare like fractions, you compare:
Comparing Fractions.explain: Since like fractions share the same denominator, you only need to compare the numerators.

Comparing Fractions.q: Which is bigger: 5/9 or 7/9?
Comparing Fractions.explain: Both have denominator 9, so compare numerators: 7 > 5, making 7/9 bigger.

Comparing Fractions.q: Compare 3/8 and 6/8. Which fraction is larger? (write just the fraction)
Comparing Fractions.explain: Both have denominator 8, and 6 > 3, so 6/8 is larger.

Comparing Fractions.q: What are unlike fractions?
To compare unlike fractions, the first step is to:
opts: Convert them to like fractions using the LCM of denominators
Comparing Fractions.explain: Converting unlike fractions to like fractions (using LCM) lets you compare numerators fairly.

Comparing Fractions.q: What is the LCM of the denominators 4 and 6, used to compare fractions with these denominators?
Comparing Fractions.explain: The LCM of 4 and 6 is 12 (the smallest number divisible by both).

Comparing Fractions.q: Comparing 2/3 and 3/4 using LCM 12: which is bigger?
Compare 1/2 and 3/8 using a common denominator of 8. Which fraction is larger? (write just the fraction)
Comparing Fractions.explain: 1/2=4/8, and comparing with 3/8: since 4 > 3, 1/2 (or 4/8) is larger.

Comparing Fractions.q: A quick trick for comparing two fractions a/b and c/d is cross-multiplication: compare:
Comparing Fractions.explain: Cross-multiplication compares a×d with b×c to quickly determine which fraction is larger.

Comparing Fractions.q: To order three or more unlike fractions, you should:
opts: Convert all to like fractions using the LCM of all denominators, then compare numerators
Comparing Fractions.explain: Converting all fractions to a common denominator (LCM) allows fair comparison of all numerators at once.

Comparing Fractions.q: Arrange these like fractions from SMALLEST to LARGEST: 7/10, 2/10, 5/10.
Comparing Fractions.explain: Comparing numerators with the same denominator: 2 < 5 < 7, so order is 2/10, 5/10, 7/10.

Comparing Fractions.q: Two glasses are filled with juice: Glass A has 3/5 full, Glass B has 4/5 full. Which glass has more juice?
Comparing Fractions.explain: Both have denominator 5, and 4 > 3, so Glass B has more juice.

Comparing Fractions.q: Rohan read 2/3 of a book and Meena read 5/6 of the same book. Using LCM 6, what is 2/3 written as sixths?
Continuing the previous scenario: who read more of the book, Rohan (2/3 = 4/6) or Meena (5/6)?
Comparing Fractions.explain: Comparing 4/6 and 5/6 with the same denominator: 5 > 4, so Meena read more.

Comparing Fractions.q: Two ropes are cut: Rope A is 5/8 of a metre, Rope B is 3/4 of a metre. What is 3/4 written with denominator 8?
Continuing the previous scenario: which rope is longer, Rope A (5/8m) or Rope B (6/8m)?
Comparing Fractions.explain: Comparing 5/8 and 6/8: since 6 > 5, Rope B (3/4m) is longer.

Comparing Fractions.q: When ordering fractions from LARGEST to SMALLEST after converting to like fractions, you should:
opts: List numerators from smallest to largest
List numerators from largest to smallest
Comparing Fractions.explain: For largest to smallest order, arrange the converted numerators in decreasing order.

Comparing Fractions.q: Three friends ran 1/2 km, 1/3 km, and 5/6 km. Using LCM 6, write 1/2 as sixths.
Using the previous scenario (1/2=3/6, 1/3=2/6, 5/6=5/6), arrange the distances run by the three friends from LEAST to MOST.
Comparing Fractions.explain: Comparing sixths: 2/6 < 3/6 < 5/6, meaning 1/3 km < 1/2 km < 5/6 km.

Fraction of a Quantity.q: To find a fraction of a quantity, what are the two steps?
opts: Add the numerator, then subtract the denominator
Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator
Multiply by the denominator, then divide by the numerator
Fraction of a Quantity.explain: Divide the quantity by the denominator first, then multiply that result by the numerator.

Fraction of a Quantity.q: What is 1/2 of 18?
What is 1/3 of 21?
What is 3/4 of 16?
What is 2/5 of 30?
What is 5/6 of 24?
What is 3/8 of 40?
Which clue word in a problem suggests you should find a fraction OF a quantity?
Fraction of a Quantity.explain: The word "of" (as in "2/3 of the students") signals you need to find a fraction of a quantity.

Fraction of a Quantity.q: A bag has 45 marbles. If 2/9 of them are red, how many marbles are red?
A class has 36 students. If 5/6 of them passed an exam, how many students passed?
A 56km road trip is 3/7 complete. How many km have been travelled?
A recipe needs 2/3 of 27 grams of butter. How many grams is that?
Fraction of a Quantity.explain: 27÷3=9, then 9×2=18. So 2/3 of 27 grams is 18 grams.

Fraction of a Quantity.q: Why must the quantity divide evenly by the denominator for this method to give a whole-number answer?
opts: It does not need to divide evenly
Because the division step creates equal whole groups; uneven division would leave a fractional remainder per group
Because fractions can never apply to quantities
Fraction of a Quantity.explain: Dividing the quantity by the denominator creates equal-sized whole groups; if it does not divide evenly, the per-group amount becomes a fraction itself.

Fraction of a Quantity.q: Arrange the steps to find 4/5 of 35.
Fraction of a Quantity.explain: First divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator, then state the result.

Fraction of a Quantity.q: A ₹900 item is discounted by 1/3. How much is the discount amount?
Continuing the previous question, what is the FINAL price of the ₹900 item after the ₹300 discount?
A water tank holds 72 litres. If 7/12 of it is currently filled, how many litres of water are in the tank?
Fraction of a Quantity.explain: 72÷12=6, then 6×7=42. So 42 litres are in the tank.

Fraction of a Quantity.q: A farmer has 63 mangoes. If 4/9 of them are sold, how many mangoes are sold?
A library has 80 books. If 3/10 are fiction, how many books are NOT fiction?
Fraction of a Quantity.explain: 80÷10=8, then 8×3=24 fiction books. So 80−24=56 books are not fiction.

Fraction of a Quantity.q: A 48-minute movie has 5/8 of it already watched. How many minutes have been watched?
Fraction of a Quantity.explain: 48÷8=6, then 6×5=30. So 30 minutes have been watched.

Addition & Subtraction of Fractions.q: To add two like fractions, you:
opts: Add the numerators and keep the denominator the same
Addition & Subtraction of Fractions.explain: For like fractions, add the numerators and keep the common denominator unchanged.

Addition & Subtraction of Fractions.q: What is 2/7 + 3/7?
What is 4/9 + 3/9?
To subtract two like fractions, you:
opts: Subtract the numerators and keep the denominator the same
Addition & Subtraction of Fractions.explain: For like fractions, subtract the numerators and keep the common denominator unchanged.

Addition & Subtraction of Fractions.q: What is 7/8 − 3/8?
Addition & Subtraction of Fractions.explain: Subtract numerators: 7−3=4, keep denominator 8, giving 4/8 (simplifies to 1/2).
Subtract numerators: 9−4=5, keep denominator 10, giving 5/10 (simplifies to 1/2).

Addition & Subtraction of Fractions.q: To add unlike fractions, the first step is to:
opts: Find the LCM of the denominators and convert to like fractions
Subtract the smaller denominator from the larger
Addition & Subtraction of Fractions.explain: Unlike fractions must first be converted to like fractions using the LCM of their denominators.

Addition & Subtraction of Fractions.q: Find the LCM of 4 and 6 (needed to add 1/4 + 1/6).
What is 2/3 + 1/6 (using LCM 6: 2/3=4/6)?
What is 3/4 − 1/2 (using LCM 4: 1/2=2/4)?
What is 5/6 − 1/3 (using LCM 6: 1/3=2/6)?
When adding mixed fractions, the best first step is to:
opts: Add only the whole number parts
Convert each mixed fraction into an improper fraction first
Addition & Subtraction of Fractions.explain: Converting mixed fractions to improper fractions first makes the addition process consistent and simple.

Addition & Subtraction of Fractions.q: Arrange the steps to solve 1/2 + 1/3.
Addition & Subtraction of Fractions.explain: First find the LCM, then convert both fractions, then add to get the final result.

Addition & Subtraction of Fractions.q: Aman ate 2/5 of a cake and his sister ate 1/5 of the same cake. What fraction of the cake did they eat together?
A tank is 3/4 full of water. If 1/4 of the tank’s water is used, what fraction remains?
Addition & Subtraction of Fractions.explain: 3/4 − 1/4 = 2/4 (which simplifies to 1/2) of the tank remains.

Addition & Subtraction of Fractions.q: Priya walked 1/3 km in the morning and 1/4 km in the evening. Using LCM 12, what total fraction of a km did she walk?
A bottle had 5/6 litre of juice. After drinking 1/2 litre (using LCM 6: 1/2=3/6), how much juice remains?
A painter used 2 1/2 litres of paint on Monday and 1 1/4 litres on Tuesday. As improper fractions, these are 5/2 and 5/4. Using LCM 4, what is 5/2 written as fourths?
Continuing the painter scenario (5/2=10/4 litres Monday, 5/4 litres Tuesday), what is the total paint used as an improper fraction?

Word Problems / Mixed Practice.q: In a word problem, the phrase "altogether" or "in total" usually signals which operation?
opts: Multiplication of a fraction by a quantity
Word Problems / Mixed Practice.explain: "Altogether" and "in total" typically mean you should add the given fractions or quantities.

Word Problems / Mixed Practice.q: In a word problem, the phrase "how much is left" usually signals which operation?
Word Problems / Mixed Practice.explain: "How much is left" or "remaining" signals subtraction — subtracting what was used from the total.

Word Problems / Mixed Practice.q: In a word problem, the phrase "2/5 of the workers" usually signals which approach?
opts: Finding a fraction of a quantity (divide then multiply)
Word Problems / Mixed Practice.explain: "X/Y of [a quantity]" signals finding a fraction of that quantity using the divide-then-multiply method.

Word Problems / Mixed Practice.q: Aman ate 1/6 of a cake on Monday and 2/6 on Tuesday. What fraction did he eat in total?
A water tank is 7/8 full. If 3/8 of the tank’s water is used, what fraction remains?
A 40-page assignment has 3/8 of its pages completed. How many pages are completed?
A 50m rope has 1/5 cut off, then 1/4 of what REMAINS is cut off again. How much rope is cut off in the FIRST cut?
Word Problems / Mixed Practice.explain: 1/5 of 50 = 50÷5=10m cut off in the first cut.

Word Problems / Mixed Practice.q: Continuing the previous question, how much rope remains after the FIRST cut (50m rope, 10m cut off)?
Continuing the previous question, how much rope is cut off in the SECOND cut (1/4 of the remaining 40m)?
Word Problems / Mixed Practice.explain: 1/4 of 40 = 40÷4=10m cut off in the second cut.

Word Problems / Mixed Practice.q: A 32-litre tank loses 1/4 of its water, then 1/2 of what remains is used for cleaning. How much water is used for cleaning?
Word Problems / Mixed Practice.explain: 1/4 of 32 = 8 litres lost, leaving 24 litres. Then 1/2 of 24 = 12 litres used for cleaning.

Word Problems / Mixed Practice.q: Priya has ₹720. She spends 1/3 on a book and 1/4 on a pen. What fraction of her money has she spent in total (using LCM 12)?
Continuing the previous question, how much money (in rupees) has Priya spent if 7/12 of her ₹720 is spent?
A 60-question test has 1/3 multiple-choice and 1/4 true/false; the rest are descriptive. What fraction of questions are descriptive (using LCM 12)?
Continuing the previous question, how many of the 60 questions are descriptive (5/12 of 60)?
When a word problem has MULTIPLE steps, what is the best strategy?
opts: Solve one step at a time, using each answer in the next step
Add all the numbers in the problem together
Word Problems / Mixed Practice.explain: Breaking a multi-step problem into smaller individual steps, using one answer to inform the next, avoids confusion and errors.

Word Problems / Mixed Practice.q: A baker had 5/6 kg of flour, used 1/3 kg for one recipe (using LCM 6: 1/3=2/6). How much flour remains?
A school has 200 students. 2/5 walk to school, 1/4 cycle, and the rest take the bus. What fraction takes the bus (using LCM 20)?
Continuing the previous scenario, how many of the 200 students take the bus, if that fraction is 7/20?
A 90-minute exam allows 2/5 of the time for Section A and 3/10 of the time for Section B. What fraction of the time is left for Section C (using LCM 10)?
Word Problems / Mixed Practice.explain: 2/5=4/10 and 3/10=3/10, so 4/10+3/10=7/10 used for A and B, leaving 10/10−7/10=3/10 for Section C.

Word Problems / Mixed Practice.q: Continuing the previous question, how many minutes does Section C get if it is 3/10 of the 90-minute exam?

Tenths & Hundredths.q: What is a decimal point used for?
opts: To separate the whole number part from the fractional part
Tenths & Hundredths.explain: The decimal point separates the whole number part from the decimal (fractional) part.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: In the number 6.8, which part is the whole number part?
Tenths & Hundredths.explain: 6 is the whole number part, and 8 is the decimal part.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: In the decimal 5.27, which digit is in the tenths place?
Tenths & Hundredths.explain: The first digit after the decimal point (2) is in the tenths place.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: In the decimal 5.27, which digit is in the hundredths place?
Tenths & Hundredths.explain: The second digit after the decimal point (7) is in the hundredths place.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: A strip of 10 equal parts has 4 shaded. Write this as a decimal.
Tenths & Hundredths.explain: 4 out of 10 parts shaded is 4/10, written as 0.4.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: A 10x10 grid of 100 squares has 23 shaded. Write this as a decimal.
Tenths & Hundredths.explain: 23 out of 100 squares shaded is 23/100, written as 0.23.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: Why is a zero needed when writing 7/100 as a decimal (0.07)?
opts: To hold the empty tenths place, since there are no full tenths
To make the number look bigger
Tenths & Hundredths.explain: Since 7 hundredths has no full tenths, a zero must hold the tenths place, giving 0.07.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: Arrange the place values after the decimal point from LEFT to RIGHT.
Tenths & Hundredths.explain: Reading left to right after the decimal point: tenths, then hundredths, then thousandths.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: How do you read the decimal 0.09 in words?
Tenths & Hundredths.explain: Each digit after the decimal point is read separately: zero point zero nine.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: A ribbon is divided into 10 equal strips, and a tailor uses 7 strips. What decimal of the ribbon was used?
Tenths & Hundredths.explain: 7 out of 10 strips is 7/10, written as the decimal 0.7.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: A wall is painted in 100 equal sections, and 65 sections are done. What decimal of the wall is painted?
Tenths & Hundredths.explain: 65 out of 100 sections is 65/100, written as 0.65.

Tenths & Hundredths.q: On a number line between 0 and 1 split into tenths, where would 0.6 be marked?
opts: Six-tenths of the way from 0 to 1
Tenths & Hundredths.explain: 0.6 sits six-tenths of the way between 0 and 1 on a number line divided into tenths.

opts: Yes — adding a trailing zero does not change the value
Comparing Decimals.explain: Trailing zeros after the decimal part do not change the value, so 0.4 = 0.40.

Comparing Decimals.q: Write an equivalent decimal for 0.7 with two decimal digits.
Comparing Decimals.explain: Adding a trailing zero gives 0.70, which equals 0.7.
9/10 has 1 digit after the dot, giving the decimal 0.9.
0.45 has 2 decimal digits, so it becomes 45/100.
17/100 has 2 digits after the dot, giving the decimal 0.17.

Comparing Decimals.q: When comparing decimals, which part do you compare FIRST?
Comparing Decimals.explain: Always compare the whole number parts first; only move to the tenths digit if those are equal.
Comparing tenths: 6 > 5, so 5.6 (written as 5.60) is greater than 5.58.

Comparing Decimals.q: Which is greater: 3.07 or 3.7? Write the bigger one.
Comparing Decimals.explain: Comparing tenths: 7 > 0, so 3.7 is greater than 3.07.

Comparing Decimals.q: Why is it helpful to give decimals the SAME number of decimal digits before comparing them?
opts: It makes comparing place by place easier and avoids mistakes
It changes the value to make comparison fair
Comparing Decimals.explain: Giving equal decimal digits (using trailing zeros) lines up the place values so you can compare safely, without changing any value.

Comparing Decimals.q: Arrange these decimals from SMALLEST to LARGEST: 2.5, 2.05, 2.55.
Arrange these decimals from LARGEST to SMALLEST: 0.8, 0.18, 0.08.
Comparing Decimals.explain: Comparing: 0.80 > 0.18 > 0.08, so the order from largest to smallest is 0.8, 0.18, 0.08.

Comparing Decimals.q: Two friends measure their pencils: 12.5 cm and 12.45 cm. Whose pencil is longer?
Comparing Decimals.explain: Comparing tenths: 5 > 4, so 12.5 cm (12.50 cm) is longer than 12.45 cm.

Using Decimals in Money & Length.explain: 100 paise make 1 rupee, just like 100 hundredths make 1 whole.

Using Decimals in Money & Length.q: Write ₹12 and 30 paise using a decimal.
Using Decimals in Money & Length.explain: 30 paise = 30/100 rupees = 0.30 rupees, so it is written as ₹12.30.

Using Decimals in Money & Length.q: How many paise are there in ₹8.05?
Using Decimals in Money & Length.explain: The decimal part .05 means 5 paise (5/100 of a rupee).

Using Decimals in Money & Length.q: Why should money amounts always be written with exactly 2 decimal digits?
opts: It is just a style choice
Because there are 100 paise in a rupee, so 2 digits represent the paise correctly
Using Decimals in Money & Length.explain: Since 100 paise = 1 rupee, exactly 2 decimal digits are needed to show the paise part correctly.
10 mm make 1 cm, similar to how tenths relate to a whole.
100 cm make 1 m, similar to how hundredths relate to a whole.

Using Decimals in Money & Length.q: Write 9 cm and 4 mm using a decimal (in cm).
Using Decimals in Money & Length.explain: 4 mm = 4/10 cm = 0.4 cm, so 9 cm and 4 mm is 9.4 cm.

Using Decimals in Money & Length.q: Write 5 m and 70 cm using a decimal (in metres).
A shopkeeper sells rice at ₹42.50 per kg. What does the .50 represent?
Using Decimals in Money & Length.explain: The decimal part .50 represents 50 paise, which is half a rupee.

Using Decimals in Money & Length.q: A road is 2.65 km long. What does the .65 part mean in terms of metres (1 km = 1000 m)?

Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.q: What is the FIRST step when adding or subtracting decimals?
Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.explain: Lining up the decimal points ensures digits of the same place value are added or subtracted together.

Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.q: Why do we add trailing zeros before subtracting decimals like 8 − 3.45?
opts: To make both numbers have the same number of decimal digits, for easy column subtraction
Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.explain: Writing 8 as 8.00 gives both numbers the same number of decimal digits, making column-by-column subtraction accurate.

Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.q: Riya buys a notebook for ₹35.50 and a pen for ₹12.75. What is the total cost?
Continuing the previous question, if Riya pays with a ₹50 note, how much change does she get?
A jug holds 1.5 litres of juice. If 0.65 litres is poured out, how much juice is left?
In a word problem, the word 'altogether' usually signals which operation?
In a word problem, the phrase 'how much is left' usually signals which operation?
Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.explain: 'How much is left' or 'remaining' signals subtraction.

Addition & Subtraction of Decimals.q: A tailor has 4.5 m of cloth and uses 2.85 m for a shirt. How much cloth remains?

Place Value & Expanded Form of Decimals.q: In the decimal 6.372, which place is the digit 7 in?
